Can I have a fulfilled heart if there is a vision, a hope, and or a dream in my life that lies barren and unrealized? Must I go through life carrying a cross of pain and loneliness while God answers the prayers of my friends and gives them the desires of their hearts? Is something wrong with me? Is my faith too weak? Have I not prayed enough, surrendered enough, been obedient enough? What is life all about? Why don’t I have peace and joy? Does God have a plan and a purpose for me?

“Thou wilt shew me the path of life: in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore” (Psalms 16:11).

“And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper” (Psalms 1:3).

God has a path provided for each of us that will lead to a fulfilled heart. In God’s presence, there is fullness of joy! God’s desire is that your heart would be like a riverside tree, filled with life, health, strength, and fruit. He desires that you experience grace, joy, and peace, in your everyday life. God wants to fill your heart with his desires and purposes. He longs for you to seek after his will and plan. If you walk on his pathway, you will be filled with blessing and grace. This does not mean that every desire that you may have comes to pass (I don’t think that will ever happen for anyone in this life) but rather that your heart is full of the blessings of God. Your heart does not need to feel like a desert, the Water of Life can fill it.

“But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14).

Where does Fulfillment Begin?

Fulfillment starts in your relationship with God. Does He feel cold and distant to you, or do you find joy and peace in praying and walking with him? Do you know that your sins are forgiven and that you are accepted as His child? Do you obey God with a willing heart or are there areas in your life where you resist his will as revealed in the Bible? Walking in the love and grace of God is the most important thing you can do in life. This is the first step on the pathway to a fulfilled heart.

If you are struggling in your relationship with God and are not sure of his love, forgiveness, and acceptance, here are some directions from the Bible for you.

“But the righteousness which is of faith speaketh on this wise, Say not in thine heart, Who shall ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down from above:) 7 Or, Who shall descend into the deep? (that is, to bring up Christ again from the dead.) 8 But what saith it? The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach; 9 That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved. 10 For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation” (Romans 10:6-10).

You should never think that Christ is in some unapproachable place, and unavailable to you. Christ is made known to you by the Bible, his Holy Spirit, and by his creation. Unbelief, sin, disobedience, and unforgiveness to others can keep you from experiencing his love and grace. Opening your heart to Him by faith, believing in your heart, and confessing with your mouth the Lord Jesus, will restore your relationship with God. He will wash away your sin and receive you as his child. Christ came to this earth to reconcile us to God. He paid the price of our sin and guilt. We can receive his gift of salvation through faith and repentance. Faith is simply hearing the Word of God and receiving it into our hearts.

As we receive the Word of God into our hearts, it enables us to be obedient to his will. We choose to believe all that God has spoken to us in the Bible. We let go of all our doubts and embrace His Word. Repentance is turning away from our own selfish will and our sinful ways and choosing to obey God and his Word. In 1 John 1:9 God has said that if we confess our sins, He will forgive us. Do you truly believe this? Is it hard for you to accept that he will forgive you? It is impossible for God to lie, therefore his Word and promises can always be trusted.

Practical ways to walk with God

“There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit” (Romans 8:1).

There are spiritual prerequisites needed to walk with God. If we don’t have a right heart, these practical things won’t actually help us walk with God. It will only be an empty activity with no real meaning and little benefit.

With our hearts full of faith and love we need to believe everything in the Bible. We need to believe all its history, everything it says about the man, Jesus, all the prophecies, and all the direction God gives us in the Word.

We also need a surrendered heart and choose to follow and obey God in everything. There is no area in which we choose to neglect or disobey. We need to have confessed our sins and be born again by the Spirit of God.

Pray. For yourself, God’s kingdom, your family, the church, neighbors, widows and widowers, orphans, missionaries, governments, and the sick. Pray for people who have lost loved ones, hungry people, people in prison, and people who need salvation. Pray for God to send workers into the vineyard.

Study the Word. Memorize it and read it to others. Discuss it.

Sing praises to God! God has been so merciful to you. Rejoice in your salvation!

“And that the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy; as it is written, For this cause I will confess to thee among the Gentiles, and sing unto thy name. 10 And again he saith, Rejoice, ye Gentiles, with his people. 11 And again, Praise the Lord, all ye Gentiles; and laud him, all ye people” (Romans 15:9).

Contentment

Another big step in the pathway to a fulfilled heart is contentment. You can never be fulfilled if you aren’t content in knowing that you are in the will of God.

“Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee. 6 So that we may boldly say, The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me” (Hebrews 13:5).

What is covetousness? My definition of covetousness is having a strong desire for something that is outside of God’s will for me right now. Normally, covetousness will drive you to violate scripture and God’s will, to try to obtain the thing you have a desire for. For instance, if you are covetous of money, you will tend to do unethical things or neglect to follow the direction in the Bible in your pursuit of money. You may cheat, steal, scam, overcharge, or become a workaholic and neglect God, family, church, or the needy.

God has given us desires, and it is a good thing to pursue them if our heart is surrendered, seeking God’s will and pursuing it according to the direction given in the Bible. Seek to move forward, but never force your own will. Be open to the people that God has put in your life for direction.

You may be at the age when your friends are getting married. You also desire to get married, but all the doors slam shut in your face. It seems like God reveals his will to others but not you. Know that an unanswered prayer is an answer for you right here, right now.

God reveals his will to you day by day and moment by moment. Married people don’t know the long-term will of God for their lives any more than unmarried people. The reality is that my family could be taken away from me in an instant. No one is promised anything earthly for tomorrow. God promises us spiritual blessings but not physical or earthly ones.

Be careful with your expectations. You can create many hardships for yourself if you are very strong in your expectations. As an example, Matthew 20 has the story of the householder who promised his workers a penny for a day’s work. Later in the day, he hired other workers. In the evening, he was paying his workers, starting with the ones hired last, and gave them each a penny. Because of his generosity, the first workers expected more than he had promised them. Since they expected him to give them more than a penny, they murmured against him. Never have strong expectations for things that God hasn’t promised in the Bible, even if you feel like God has revealed it to you by his Spirit. It is far better to have a humble, open heart to God, family, and the brotherhood.

Fellowship

Fellowship with God’s people is another important step in the pathway to fulfillment. Don’t isolate yourself, but rather make yourself a part of God’s people.

“Then they that gladly received his word were baptized: and the same day there were added unto them about three thousand souls. 42 And they continued steadfastly in the apostles’ doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers” (Acts 2:41).

It can be easy to fall into the trap of feeling like you are different from everyone else and don’t fit in. Remember that everyone is unique, and together we make up the body of Christ. You are an important member and have gifts and abilities that are needed in your local fellowship. Spend time with people and find ways to be a blessing and help others.

Identity

Embrace your identity. You may wonder, who am I? Where do I fit in? This can be especially difficult if you have a strong desire to be married but are not. You might see others as becoming something that you desire to be but are not.

You might wonder, what is wrong with me that I am not married? This is wrong thinking. The reality is that there are many married people who are in a worse place than you. Be open when those around you have thoughts about changes you can and should make in your life, but don’t condemn yourself as not good enough and that others do not accept you. Ephesians chapter 1 says that you are chosen by God to be washed of your sins through the blood of Jesus and to be adopted as His child. You are accepted by God, and you are to be “to the praise of his glory!”

Purpose

The last step I am writing about is about purpose. What is one thing that you really enjoy doing that is a blessing to the church or Kingdom? God has a purpose for you to fulfill. You are a part of His kingdom that you can put time and energy into. God has called each one of us to be a servant, to follow in the footsteps of our Lord Jesus. It can be as simple as giving a glass of cold water in the name of Jesus. No task is too small or mundane to be a part of His kingdom. Be available. Have the heart of a servant. When you see a need, offer a helping hand or a listening ear.

“Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others. 5 Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus: 6 Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God: 7 But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men:” (Philippians 2:4)My wife and I recently celebrated our third anniversary. I was 38 and Jena 29 when we got married. This past spring we were blessed with a sweet little girl, Gianna. I wish I could say that we always lived out the things that I wrote in this article, but we are human and did come short at times. But we can both say from experience that the things I wrote are real and true. There is a pathway to joy and fulfillment as an unmarried person. Jena pursued midwifery and sacrificed a lot to serve mothers and babies. Always ready to drop whatever she was doing or jump out of bed in the middle of the night to go serve. I did a lot of Bible studies and also trips to the Middle East to study the Bible in a different measure. God has graciously given me the privilege to visit places where few people have been. I’ve been able to see where many of the people in the Bible lived and walked, including Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, David, and, best of all, Jesus. These people left behind a witness of faith and obedience. Let us follow them!

“Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us, 2 Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God. 3 For consider him that endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, lest ye be wearied and faint in your minds . . . (Hebrews 12:1-3).

“Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees; 13 And make straight paths for your feet, lest that which is lame be turned out of the way; but let it rather be healed. 14 Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord: 15 Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled . . . (Hebrews 12:12-15)

“Wherefore we receiving a kingdom which cannot be moved, let us have grace, whereby we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear” (Hebrews 12;28).

Posso ter um coração realizado se há uma visão, uma esperança ou um sonho na minha vida que jaz estéril e não realizado? Devo passar a vida carregando uma cruz de dor e solidão enquanto Deus responde às orações dos meus amigos e lhes dá os desejos dos seus corações? Há algo de errado comigo? A minha fé é fraca demais? Nãorei o suficiente, não me rendi o bastante, não fui obediente o bastante? Do que se trata a vida? Por que não tenho paz e alegria? Deus tem um plano e um propósito para mim?

“Tu me mostrarás o caminho da vida: na tua presença há plenitude de alegria; à tua mão direita há delícias perpetuamente” (Salmos 16:11).

“E será como a árvore plantada junto a ribeiros de águas, a qual dá o seu fruto no seu tempo; e a sua folha também não murchará; e tudo quanto fizer prosperará” (Salmos 1:3).

Deus providenciou um caminho para cada um de nós que conduzirá a um coração realizado. Na presença de Deus há plenitude de alegria! O desejo de Deus é que o teu coração seja como uma árvore à beira do rio, cheio de vida, saúde, força e fruto. Ele deseja que tu experimentes graça, alegria e paz no teu dia a dia. Deus quer encher o teu coração com os seus desejos e propósitos. Ele anseia que procures a sua vontade e plano. Se andares no seu caminho, serás cheio de bênção e graça. Isso não significa que todo desejo que possas ter se realizará (não creio que isso aconteça para alguém nesta vida), mas sim que o teu coração está cheio das bênçãos de Deus. O teu coração não precisa parecer um deserto; a Água da Vida pode enchê-lo.

“Mas aquele que beber da água que eu lhe der nunca terá sede; pelo contrário, a água que eu lhe der será nele uma fonte de água que salte para a vida eterna” (João 4:14).

Onde começa a realização?

A realização começa no teu relacionamento com Deus. Ele te parece frio e distante, ou tu encontras alegria e paz ao orar e andar com ele? Sabes que os teus pecados são perdoados e que és aceito como seu filho? Obedece a Deus com um coração disposto ou há áreas na tua vida em que resistes à sua vontade tal como revelada na Bíblia? Andar no amor e na graça de Deus é a coisa mais importante que podes fazer na vida. Este é o primeiro passo no caminho para um coração realizado.

Se estás lutando no teu relacionamento com Deus e não tens certeza do seu amor, perdão e aceitação, aqui estão algumas direções da Bíblia para ti.

“Mas a justiça que vem da fé fala assim: Não digas no teu coração: Quem subirá ao céu? (isto é, para fazer descer a Cristo); 7 Ou: Quem descerá ao abismo? (isto é, para fazer subir a Cristo dentre os mortos). 8 Mas que diz? A palavra está perto de ti, na tua boca e no teu coração; isto é, a palavra da fé que pregamos; 9 Que, se com a tua boca confessares a Jesus como Senhor e em teu coração creres que Deus o ressuscitou dentre os mortos, serás salvo. 10 Porque com o coração se crê para a justiça; e com a boca se faz confissão para a salvação” (Romanos 10:6-10).

Não deves jamais pensar que Cristo está em algum lugar inalcançável e indisponível para ti. Cristo é conhecido por ti pela Bíblia, pelo seu Espírito Santo e pela sua criação. A incredulidade, o pecado, a desobediência e a falta de perdão para com os outros podem impedir-te de experimentar o seu amor e graça. Abrir o teu coração para Ele pela fé, crer no teu coração e confessar com a tua boca o Senhor Jesus restaurará o teu relacionamento com Deus. Ele lavará o teu pecado e te receberá como seu filho. Cristo veio a esta terra para nos reconciliar com Deus. Ele pagou o preço do nosso pecado e culpa. Podemos receber o seu dom de salvação por meio da fé e do arrependimento. Fé é simplesmente ouvir a Palavra de Deus e recebê-la em nossos corações.

Ao recebermos a Palavra de Deus em nossos corações, ela nos capacita a obedecer à sua vontade. Nós escolhemos crer em tudo o que Deus nos falou na Bíblia. Largamos todas as nossas dúvidas e abraçamos a Sua Palavra. Arrependimento é afastar-se da nossa própria vontade egoísta e dos nossos caminhos pecaminosos e escolher obedecer a Deus e à sua Palavra. Em 1 João 1:9 Deus disse que, se confessarmos os nossos pecados, Ele nos perdoará. Tu realmente acreditas nisso? É difícil para ti aceitar que ele te perdoará? É impossível para Deus mentir, portanto a sua Palavra e promessas são sempre confiáveis.

Maneiras práticas de andar com Deus

“Portanto, agora já nenhuma condenação há para os que estão em Cristo Jesus, que não andam segundo a carne, mas segundo o Espírito” (Romanos 8:1).

Existem pré-requisitos espirituais necessários para andar com Deus. Se não tivermos um coração correto, essas coisas práticas não nos ajudarão realmente a andar com Deus. Serão apenas uma atividade vazia, sem significado real e com pouco benefício.

Com os nossos corações cheios de fé e amor, precisamos crer em tudo que está na Bíblia. Precisamos crer em toda a sua história, em tudo o que diz sobre o homem, Jesus, em todas as profecias e em toda a direção que Deus nos dá na Palavra.

Também precisamos de um coração rendido e escolher seguir e obedecer a Deus em tudo. Não deve haver área em que escolhamos negligenciar ou desobedecer. Precisamos ter confessado os nossos pecados e nascermos de novo pelo Espírito de Deus.

Ore. Por ti mesmo, pelo reino de Deus, pela tua família, pela igreja, pelos vizinhos, por viúvas e viúvos, órfãos, missionários, governos e pelos enfermos. Ore por pessoas que perderam entes queridos, por famintos, por presos e por pessoas que precisam de salvação. Ore para que Deus envie trabalhadores para a sua vinha.

Estude a Palavra. Memorize-a e leia-a a outros. Discutam-na.

Cante louvores a Deus! Deus tem sido tão misericordioso contigo. Alegra-te na tua salvação!

“E que os gentios glorificassem a Deus por sua misericórdia; como está escrito: Pelo que te confessarei entre os gentios, e cantarei ao teu nome. 10 E outra vez diz: Alegrai-vos, ó gentios, com o seu povo. 11 E outra vez: Louvai ao Senhor, todos os gentios; e louvai-o todos os povos” (Romanos 15:9).

Contentamento

Outro grande passo no caminho para um coração realizado é o contentamento. Nunca poderás estar realizado se não estiveres contente em saber que estás na vontade de Deus.

“Seja a vossa conversa sem avareza; e sede contentes com as coisas que tendes; porque ele tem dito: Não te deixarei, nem te desampararei. 6 De maneira que com boa coragem digamos: O Senhor é o meu ajudador; e não temerei o que me possa fazer o homem” (Hebreus 13:5).

O que é avareza? A minha definição de avareza é ter um forte desejo por algo que está fora da vontade de Deus para mim neste momento. Normalmente, a avareza levar-te-á a violar a Escritura e a vontade de Deus, na tentativa de obter aquilo que desejas. Por exemplo, se és avarento por dinheiro, tenderás a fazer coisas antiéticas ou a negligenciar seguir a direção da Bíblia na tua busca por dinheiro. Podes enganar, roubar, fraudar, cobrar em excesso ou tornar-te um workaholic e negligenciar a Deus, a família, a igreja ou os necessitados.

Deus nos deu desejos, e é algo bom persegui-los se o nosso coração estiver rendido, buscando a vontade de Deus e perseguindo-a de acordo com a direção dada na Bíblia. Procura avançar, mas nunca forces a tua própria vontade. Sê receptivo às pessoas que Deus colocou em tua vida para te dar direção.

Podes estar numa idade em que os teus amigos estão a casar-se. Também desejas casar, mas todas as portas se fecham na tua cara. Parece que Deus revela a sua vontade aos outros, mas não a ti. Saiba que uma oração não respondida é uma resposta para ti aqui e agora.

Deus revela a sua vontade a ti dia a dia e momento a momento. Pessoas casadas não sabem a vontade de Deus a longo prazo para as suas vidas mais do que pessoas não casadas. A realidade é que a minha família poderia ser tirada de mim num instante. Ninguém tem a promessa de qualquer coisa terrena para o amanhã. Deus nos promete bênçãos espirituais, mas não promessas físicas ou terrenas.

Sê cuidadoso com as tuas expectativas. Podes criar muitas dificuldades para ti mesmo se fores muito forte nas tuas expectativas. Como exemplo, Mateus 20 traz a história do senhor da vinha que prometeu aos seus trabalhadores um denário por um dia de trabalho. Mais tarde, naquele dia, ele contratou outros trabalhadores. À tarde, ao pagar os trabalhadores, começou pelos últimos contratados e deu a cada um um denário. Por causa da sua generosidade, os primeiros trabalhadores esperavam mais do que ele lhes havia prometido. Como esperavam que lhes fosse dado mais que um denário, eles murmuraram contra ele. Nunca tenhas expectativas fortes por coisas que Deus não prometeu na Bíblia, mesmo que sintas que Deus te revelou isso pelo seu Espírito. É muito melhor ter um coração humilde e aberto para com Deus, a família e a irmandade.

Comunhão

A comunhão com o povo de Deus é outro passo importante no caminho para a realização. Não te isoles; antes, faz parte do povo de Deus.

“Então os que com alegria receberam a sua palavra foram batizados; e naquele dia houve acrescentados quase três mil almas. 42 E perseveravam na doutrina dos apóstolos, na comunhão, no partir do pão e nas orações” (Atos 2:41).

Pode ser fácil cair na armadilha de sentir que és diferente de toda a gente e não te encaixas. Lembra-te de que cada um é único e, juntos, constituímos o corpo de Cristo. Tu és um membro importante e tens dons e habilidades que são necessários na tua comunhão local. Passa tempo com as pessoas e encontra maneiras de ser uma bênção e ajudar os outros.

Identidade

Abrace a tua identidade. Podes perguntar: quem sou eu? Onde me encaixo? Isso pode ser especialmente difícil se tens um forte desejo de casar e não o és. Podes ver outros a tornarem-se aquilo que desejas ser, mas não és.

Poderás perguntar-te, o que há de errado comigo por eu não ser casado? Esse é um pensamento errado. A realidade é que há muitos casados que estão numa situação pior do que tu. Sê receptivo quando aqueles à tua volta tiverem pensamentos sobre mudanças que podes e deves fazer na tua vida, mas não te condenes como não sendo bom o bastante e que os outros não te aceitam. Efésios capítulo 1 diz que foste escolhido por Deus para seres lavado dos teus pecados pelo sangue de Jesus e para seres adotado como seu filho. És aceito por Deus e deves ser “para louvor da sua glória!”

Propósito

O último passo sobre o qual escrevo trata de propósito. Qual é uma coisa que realmente gostas de fazer que é uma bênção para a igreja ou o Reino? Deus tem um propósito que quer que cumpras. Tu és parte do Seu reino no qual podes investir tempo e energia. Deus chamou cada um de nós para ser servo, para seguir os passos do nosso Senhor Jesus. Pode ser tão simples como dar um copo de água fria em nome de Jesus. Nenhuma tarefa é pequena ou mundana demais para ser parte do Seu reino. Esteja disponível. Tenha o coração de um servo. Quando vês uma necessidade, oferece uma mão amiga ou um ouvido que ouça.

“Não atente cada um para o que é propriamente seu, mas cada qual também para o que é dos outros. 5 Tende em vós o mesmo sentimento que houve também em Cristo Jesus: 6 O qual, subsistindo em forma de Deus, não julgou como usurpação o ser igual a Deus; 7 Mas aniquilou-se a si mesmo, tomando a forma de servo, feito semelhante aos homens” (Filipenses 2:4) Minha esposa e eu celebrámos recentemente o nosso terceiro aniversário. Eu tinha 38 e Jena tinha 29 quando nos casámos. Nesta primavera passada fomos abençoados com uma doce menina, Gianna. Eu gostaria de poder dizer que sempre vivemos as coisas que escrevi neste artigo, mas somos humanos e às vezes pecámos. Mas podemos ambos dizer por experiência que as coisas que escrevi são reais e verdadeiras. Há um caminho para a alegria e realização como pessoa não casada. Jena seguiu a obstetrícia e sacrificou muito para servir mães e bebés. Sempre pronta para largar o que estivesse a fazer ou saltar da cama no meio da noite para ir servir. Fiz muitos estudos bíblicos e também viagens ao Oriente Médio para estudar a Bíblia numa medida diferente. Deus graciosa­mente-me deu o privilégio de visitar lugares onde poucas pessoas estiveram. Pude ver onde muitas das pessoas da Bíblia viveram e andaram, incluindo Noé, Abraão, Isaac, Jacó, Moisés, Davi e, o melhor de todos, Jesus. Essas pessoas deixaram um testemunho de fé e obediência. Sigamos o seu exemplo!

“Portanto, vendo que estamos rodeados de tão grande nuvem de testemunhas, deixemos todo o peso e o pecado que tão de perto nos assedia, e corramos com paciência a carreira que nos está proposta, 2 Olhando para Jesus, autor e consumador da fé, o qual, pelo gozo que lhe estava proposto, suportou a cruz, desprezando a afronta, e assentou-se à destra do trono de Deus. 3 Considerai aquele que suportou tal contradição de pecadores contra si mesmo, para que não vos canseis, desfalecendo nas vossas mentes... (Hebreus 12:1-3).

“Por isso levantai as mãos que estão caídas, e as coxas que tremem; 13 E fazei em vossos pés caminhos retos, para que o coxo não se desvie, antes seja curado. 14 Segui a paz com todos e a santificação, sem a qual ninguém verá o Senhor. 15 Olhai diligentemente que nenhum de vós deixe de alcançar a graça de Deus; que nenhuma raiz de amargura, brotando, vos perturbe, e por isso muitos sejam contaminados... (Hebreus 12:12-15)

“Por isso recebendo um reino que não pode ser abalado, retenhamos a graça pela qual possamos, servindo a Deus, agradá-lo com temor e piedade” (Hebreus 12;28).

Can I have a fulfilled heart if there is a vision, a hope, and or a dream in my life that lies barren and unrealized? Must I go through life carrying a cross of pain and loneliness while God answers the prayers of my friends and gives them the desires of their hearts? Is something wrong with me? Is my faith too weak? Have I not prayed enough, surrendered enough, been obedient enough? What is life all about? Why don’t I have peace and joy? Does God have a plan and a purpose for me?

“Thou wilt shew me the path of life: in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore” (Psalms 16:11).

“And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper” (Psalms 1:3).

God has a path provided for each of us that will lead to a fulfilled heart. In God’s presence, there is fullness of joy! God’s desire is that your heart would be like a riverside tree, filled with life, health, strength, and fruit. He desires that you experience grace, joy, and peace, in your everyday life. God wants to fill your heart with his desires and purposes. He longs for you to seek after his will and plan. If you walk on his pathway, you will be filled with blessing and grace. This does not mean that every desire that you may have comes to pass (I don’t think that will ever happen for anyone in this life) but rather that your heart is full of the blessings of God. Your heart does not need to feel like a desert, the Water of Life can fill it.

“But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14).

Where does Fulfillment Begin?

Fulfillment starts in your relationship with God. Does He feel cold and distant to you, or do you find joy and peace in praying and walking with him? Do you know that your sins are forgiven and that you are accepted as His child? Do you obey God with a willing heart or are there areas in your life where you resist his will as revealed in the Bible? Walking in the love and grace of God is the most important thing you can do in life. This is the first step on the pathway to a fulfilled heart.

If you are struggling in your relationship with God and are not sure of his love, forgiveness, and acceptance, here are some directions from the Bible for you.

“But the righteousness which is of faith speaketh on this wise, Say not in thine heart, Who shall ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down from above:) 7 Or, Who shall descend into the deep? (that is, to bring up Christ again from the dead.) 8 But what saith it? The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach; 9 That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved. 10 For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation” (Romans 10:6-10).

You should never think that Christ is in some unapproachable place, and unavailable to you. Christ is made known to you by the Bible, his Holy Spirit, and by his creation. Unbelief, sin, disobedience, and unforgiveness to others can keep you from experiencing his love and grace. Opening your heart to Him by faith, believing in your heart, and confessing with your mouth the Lord Jesus, will restore your relationship with God. He will wash away your sin and receive you as his child. Christ came to this earth to reconcile us to God. He paid the price of our sin and guilt. We can receive his gift of salvation through faith and repentance. Faith is simply hearing the Word of God and receiving it into our hearts.

As we receive the Word of God into our hearts, it enables us to be obedient to his will. We choose to believe all that God has spoken to us in the Bible. We let go of all our doubts and embrace His Word. Repentance is turning away from our own selfish will and our sinful ways and choosing to obey God and his Word. In 1 John 1:9 God has said that if we confess our sins, He will forgive us. Do you truly believe this? Is it hard for you to accept that he will forgive you? It is impossible for God to lie, therefore his Word and promises can always be trusted.

Practical ways to walk with God

“There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit” (Romans 8:1).

There are spiritual prerequisites needed to walk with God. If we don’t have a right heart, these practical things won’t actually help us walk with God. It will only be an empty activity with no real meaning and little benefit.

With our hearts full of faith and love we need to believe everything in the Bible. We need to believe all its history, everything it says about the man, Jesus, all the prophecies, and all the direction God gives us in the Word.

We also need a surrendered heart and choose to follow and obey God in everything. There is no area in which we choose to neglect or disobey. We need to have confessed our sins and be born again by the Spirit of God.

Pray. For yourself, God’s kingdom, your family, the church, neighbors, widows and widowers, orphans, missionaries, governments, and the sick. Pray for people who have lost loved ones, hungry people, people in prison, and people who need salvation. Pray for God to send workers into the vineyard.

Study the Word. Memorize it and read it to others. Discuss it.

Sing praises to God! God has been so merciful to you. Rejoice in your salvation!

“And that the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy; as it is written, For this cause I will confess to thee among the Gentiles, and sing unto thy name. 10 And again he saith, Rejoice, ye Gentiles, with his people. 11 And again, Praise the Lord, all ye Gentiles; and laud him, all ye people” (Romans 15:9).

Contentment

Another big step in the pathway to a fulfilled heart is contentment. You can never be fulfilled if you aren’t content in knowing that you are in the will of God.

“Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee. 6 So that we may boldly say, The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me” (Hebrews 13:5).

What is covetousness? My definition of covetousness is having a strong desire for something that is outside of God’s will for me right now. Normally, covetousness will drive you to violate scripture and God’s will, to try to obtain the thing you have a desire for. For instance, if you are covetous of money, you will tend to do unethical things or neglect to follow the direction in the Bible in your pursuit of money. You may cheat, steal, scam, overcharge, or become a workaholic and neglect God, family, church, or the needy.

God has given us desires, and it is a good thing to pursue them if our heart is surrendered, seeking God’s will and pursuing it according to the direction given in the Bible. Seek to move forward, but never force your own will. Be open to the people that God has put in your life for direction.

You may be at the age when your friends are getting married. You also desire to get married, but all the doors slam shut in your face. It seems like God reveals his will to others but not you. Know that an unanswered prayer is an answer for you right here, right now.

God reveals his will to you day by day and moment by moment. Married people don’t know the long-term will of God for their lives any more than unmarried people. The reality is that my family could be taken away from me in an instant. No one is promised anything earthly for tomorrow. God promises us spiritual blessings but not physical or earthly ones.

Be careful with your expectations. You can create many hardships for yourself if you are very strong in your expectations. As an example, Matthew 20 has the story of the householder who promised his workers a penny for a day’s work. Later in the day, he hired other workers. In the evening, he was paying his workers, starting with the ones hired last, and gave them each a penny. Because of his generosity, the first workers expected more than he had promised them. Since they expected him to give them more than a penny, they murmured against him. Never have strong expectations for things that God hasn’t promised in the Bible, even if you feel like God has revealed it to you by his Spirit. It is far better to have a humble, open heart to God, family, and the brotherhood.

Fellowship

Fellowship with God’s people is another important step in the pathway to fulfillment. Don’t isolate yourself, but rather make yourself a part of God’s people.

“Then they that gladly received his word were baptized: and the same day there were added unto them about three thousand souls. 42 And they continued steadfastly in the apostles’ doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers” (Acts 2:41).

It can be easy to fall into the trap of feeling like you are different from everyone else and don’t fit in. Remember that everyone is unique, and together we make up the body of Christ. You are an important member and have gifts and abilities that are needed in your local fellowship. Spend time with people and find ways to be a blessing and help others.

Identity

Embrace your identity. You may wonder, who am I? Where do I fit in? This can be especially difficult if you have a strong desire to be married but are not. You might see others as becoming something that you desire to be but are not.

You might wonder, what is wrong with me that I am not married? This is wrong thinking. The reality is that there are many married people who are in a worse place than you. Be open when those around you have thoughts about changes you can and should make in your life, but don’t condemn yourself as not good enough and that others do not accept you. Ephesians chapter 1 says that you are chosen by God to be washed of your sins through the blood of Jesus and to be adopted as His child. You are accepted by God, and you are to be “to the praise of his glory!”

Purpose

The last step I am writing about is about purpose. What is one thing that you really enjoy doing that is a blessing to the church or Kingdom? God has a purpose for you to fulfill. You are a part of His kingdom that you can put time and energy into. God has called each one of us to be a servant, to follow in the footsteps of our Lord Jesus. It can be as simple as giving a glass of cold water in the name of Jesus. No task is too small or mundane to be a part of His kingdom. Be available. Have the heart of a servant. When you see a need, offer a helping hand or a listening ear.

“Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others. 5 Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus: 6 Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God: 7 But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men:” (Philippians 2:4)My wife and I recently celebrated our third anniversary. I was 38 and Jena 29 when we got married. This past spring we were blessed with a sweet little girl, Gianna. I wish I could say that we always lived out the things that I wrote in this article, but we are human and did come short at times. But we can both say from experience that the things I wrote are real and true. There is a pathway to joy and fulfillment as an unmarried person. Jena pursued midwifery and sacrificed a lot to serve mothers and babies. Always ready to drop whatever she was doing or jump out of bed in the middle of the night to go serve. I did a lot of Bible studies and also trips to the Middle East to study the Bible in a different measure. God has graciously given me the privilege to visit places where few people have been. I’ve been able to see where many of the people in the Bible lived and walked, including Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, David, and, best of all, Jesus. These people left behind a witness of faith and obedience. Let us follow them!

“Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us, 2 Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God. 3 For consider him that endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, lest ye be wearied and faint in your minds . . . (Hebrews 12:1-3).

“Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees; 13 And make straight paths for your feet, lest that which is lame be turned out of the way; but let it rather be healed. 14 Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord: 15 Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled . . . (Hebrews 12:12-15)

“Wherefore we receiving a kingdom which cannot be moved, let us have grace, whereby we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear” (Hebrews 12;28).

Je, ninaweza kuwa na moyo uliofurahika ikiwa kuna maono, matumaini, au ndoto maishani mwangu ambayo iko tupu na haijatimia? Je, lazima nishiwe maisha nikibeba msalaba wa maumivu na upweke wakati Mungu anajibu sala za marafiki zangu na kuwapa tamaa za mioyo yao? Je, kuna kosa kwangu? Je, imani yangu ni dhaifu sana? Je, sijalisali vya kutosha, kusalimisha vya kutosha, au kutii vya kutosha? Maisha ni kuhusu nini? Kwa nini sina amani na furaha? Je, Mungu ana mpango na kusudi kwangu?

“Utanionyesha njia ya uzima: mbele zako kuna ukamilifu wa furaha; kwa mkono wako wa kuume kuna raha milele” (Zaburi 16:11).

“Na atakuwa kama mti uliopandwa kando ya mito ya maji, ambao hutoa matunda yake kwa msimu wake; jani lake halitauka; na atakaye kosa atafanikiwa” (Zaburi 1:3).

Mungu ameandaa njia kwa kila mmoja wetu ambayo itasababisha moyo uliofurahika. Katika uwepo wa Mungu kuna ukamilifu wa furaha! Kutamani kwa Mungu ni kuwa moyo wako uwe kama mti wa kando ya mto, uliojaa uzima, afya, nguvu, na matunda. Anataka ujione ukipata neema, furaha, na amani katika maisha yako ya kila siku. Mungu anataka kujaa moyo wako kwa tamaa zake na kusudi zake. Anatamani ukiwe unamtafuta mapenzi yake na mpango wake. Ukitembea katika njia yake, utakamilishwa kwa baraka na neema. Hii haimaanishi kwamba tamaa zote utakazokuwa nazo zitatimia (sidhani hilo litamtokea mtu yeyote katika maisha haya) bali kwamba moyo wako utakamilishwa kwa baraka za Mungu. Moyo wako hauhitaji kuhisi kama jangwa, Maji ya Uzima yanaweza kuujaza.

“Lakini yeyote anayekunywa maji nitakayompa hatakasirika kamwe; bali maji nitakayompa yatakuwa ndani yake kisima cha maji kinachomiminika hadi uzima wa milele” (Yohana 4:14).

Fulfillment inaanzia wapi?

Ukamalifu unaanza katika uhusiano wako na Mungu. Je, yeye anakuonekana baridi na mbali kwako, au unapata furaha na amani katika kuomba na kutembea pamoja naye? Je, unajua kwamba dhambi zako zimesamehewa na kwamba umekubaliwa kuwa mtoto wake? Je, unamtii Mungu kwa moyo wa hiari au kuna maeneo katika maisha yako ambapo unakataa mapenzi yake kama yalivyoonyeshwa katika Biblia? Kutembea katika upendo na neema za Mungu ndiyo jambo muhimu zaidi unaloweza kufanya maishani. Huu ni hatua ya kwanza katika njia ya kupata moyo uliofurahika.

Iwapo unapata ugumu katika uhusiano wako na Mungu na huna uhakika wa upendo wake, msamaha, na kukubaliwa, hapa kuna mwelekeo kutoka katika Biblia kwako.

“Lakini haki ambayo ni ya imani husema hivi, Usisema moyoni mwako, Nani atapanda mbinguni? (yaani, kumleta Kristo kutoka juu:) 7 Au, Nani atashuka kuzimu? (yaani, kumletea Kristo tena kutoka kwa wafu.) 8 Lakini inasema nini? Neno lipo karibu nawe, hata kinywani mwako, na moyoni mwako: yaani, neno la imani, ambalo tunatoa habari; 9 Ndipo ukimtangazia kwa kinywa chako Bwana Yesu, na ukamwamini moyoni mwako kwamba Mungu amemfufua kutoka kwa wafu, utakombolewa. 10 Kwa maana kwa moyo mtu huamini kwa ajili ya haki; na kwa kinywa hutangazwa kwa ajili ya wokovu” (Warumi 10:6-10).

Hautapaswa kamwe kufikiria kwamba Kristo yuko mahali pazidi kufikiwa, na hana kwako. Kristo anafahamika kwako kupitia Biblia, Roho Mtakatifu wake, na kupitia uumbaji wake. Kukosa kuamini, dhambi, kutokuwa wafuata, na kukosekana kwa kusamehe wengine kunaweza kukuzuia upate upendo na neema yake. Kufungua moyo wako kwake kwa imani, kuamini moyoni, na kushuhudia kwa kinywa Bwana Yesu, kutarejesha uhusiano wako na Mungu. Yeye atawaoshea dhambi zako na akutakase kuwa mtoto wake. Kristo alikuja duniani kutuweka upya kwa Mungu. Alilipa bei ya dhambi zetu na hatia yetu. Tunaweza kupokea zawadi yake ya wokovu kupitia imani na toba. Imani ni kusikia Neno la Mungu na kulitia moyoni mwetu.

Tunapopokea Neno la Mungu mioyoni mwetu, linatufanya tuwe wa watiifu kwa mapenzi yake. Tunaamua kuamini yote ambayo Mungu ametuambia katika Biblia. Tunaachilia mashaka yetu yote na tukumbatie Neno lake. Toba ni kugeuka mbali na mapenzi yetu ya kibinafsi na njia zetu za dhambi na kuchagua kumtii Mungu na Neno lake. Katika 1 Yohana 1:9 Mungu amesema kwamba tukituhumiwa dhambi zetu, atatusamehe. Je, unaamini hivyo kweli? Je, ni vigumu kwako kukubali kwamba atakuachilia? Ni vigumu kwa Mungu kulegeza uwongo, kwa hiyo Neno lake na ahadi zake daima zinaweza kuaminiwa.

Njia za vitendo za kutembea na Mungu

“Basi sasa hakuna hukumu kwa wale walio katika Kristo Yesu, wasiokuwa wanatembea kwa mwili, bali kwa Roho” (Warumi 8:1).

Kuna masharti ya kiroho yanayohitajika ili kutembea na Mungu. Iwapo hatuna moyo sahihi, mambo haya ya vitendo hayatatufanya kutembea na Mungu. Itakuwa shughuli tupu bila maana ya kweli na faida ndogo.

Tukiwa na mioyo yetu iliyojaa imani na upendo tunahitaji kuamini kila kitu katika Biblia. Tunahitaji kuamini historia yake yote, kila asema kuhusu Mwanaume, Yesu, manabii yote, na maelekezo yote ambayo Mungu anatupa katika Neno.

Pia tunahitaji moyo uliyosalimishwa na kuchagua kumfuata na kumtii Mungu katika kila jambo. Hakuna eneo ambalo tunaamua kuachwa au kukataa. Tunahitaji kuwa tumeitaja dhambi zetu na kuzaliwa upya na Roho wa Mungu.

Ombeni. Kwa ajili yako mwenyewe, ufalme wa Mungu, familia yako, kanisa, majirani, wajane na wajomba, yatima, wamisionari, serikali, na wagonjwa. Ombeni kwa ajili ya watu waliopoteza wapendwa, watu wanaokosa chakula, watu gerezani, na watu wanaohitaji wokovu. Ombeni Mungu atume watumishi katika shamba la mvinyo.

Soma Neno. Ukumbuke mstari na usome kwa wengine. Jadili.

Imba sifa kwa Mungu! Mungu amekuwa mwenye rehema sana kwako. Furahieni wokovu wenu!

“Na ili mataifa yasifu Mungu kwa ajili ya rehema yake; kama ilivyoandikwa, Kwa sababu hii nitakusifu wewe miongoni mwa mataifa, nami nitaimba jina lako. 10 Na tena anasema, Furahieni ninyi mataifa pamoja na watu wake. 11 Na tena, Sifueni BWANA, ninyi mataifa yote; na kumuenziere, ninyi watu wote” (Warumi 15:9).

Kuridhika

Hatua nyingine kubwa katika njia ya moyo uliofurahika ni kuridhika. Hutaweza kamwe kukamilika ikiwa hutoridhika katika kujua kwamba uko katika mapenzi ya Mungu.

“Mwandani mwenu muwe bila tamaa ya mali; mridhike na mambo mnavyo nayo; kwa maana ame kusema, Sitakuacha wala kukutupa. 6 Kwa hivyo tunaweza kusema kwa ujasiri, Bwana ndiye msaada wangu; sitoguogopa nini mwanadamu atayenifanya” (Waebrania 13:5).

Nini ni tamaa ya mali? Ufafanuzi wangu wa tamaa ya mali ni kuwa na hamu kali ya kitu ambacho kiko nje ya mapenzi ya Mungu kwangu kwa sasa. Kawaida, tamaa ya mali itakupeleka kukiuka maandiko na mapenzi ya Mungu, kujaribu kupata kile unachokitamani. Kwa mfano, kama unataka pesa kwa tamaa, utakuwa na mwelekeo wa kufanya mambo yasiyo ya kimaadili au kukosa kufuata mwongozo wa Biblia katika kutafuta pesa. Unaweza kudanganya, kuiba, kudanganya, kutoza bei kupita kiasi, au kuwa mfanyakazi wa kupitiliza na kumwacha Mungu, familia, kanisa, au wenye uhitaji.

Mungu ametupa matamanio, na ni jambo zuri kuyafuata ikiwa moyo wetu umejisimamia, ukitafuta mapenzi ya Mungu na kuyafuata kulingana na maelekezo yaliyotolewa katika Biblia. Tafuta kusonga mbele, lakini usisukume mapenzi yako yako mwenyewe. Kuwa wazi kwa watu ambao Mungu ameweka katika maisha yako kwa ajili ya mwelekeo.

Unaweza kuwa katika umri ambapo marafiki zako wanaolewa. Pia unataka kuolewa, lakini milango yote inafungwa usoni mwako. Inaonekana Mungu anaonyesha mapenzi yake kwa wengine lakini sio kwako. Jua kwamba sala isiyojibiwa ni jibu kwako hapa sasa hivi.

Mungu anamwonyesha mapenzi yake kwako siku baada ya siku na muda kwa muda. Wanaoolewa hawajui mapenzi ya Mungu kwa muda mrefu maishani mwao zaidi kuliko wasioolewa. Ukweli ni kwamba familia yangu inaweza kuondolewa mara moja. Hakuna aliyeahidiwa kitu chochote cha duniani kwa kesho. Mungu anatuhakikishia baraka za kiroho lakini sio za kimwili au za kidunia.

Tekeleza matarajio yako kwa uangalifu. Unaweza kujenga matatizo mengi kwa mwenyewe ikiwa una matarajio makali. Kama mfano, Mathayo 20 ina hadithi ya mwenye nyumba aliyewaahidi wafanyakazi wake senti kwa siku ya kazi. Baadaye siku hiyo, alikuajiri wafanyakazi wengine. Vilevile jioni, alipokuwa akiwalipa wafanyakazi, alianza na walioajiriwa baadaye, na akawapa kila mmoja senti. Kwa ukarimu wake, wafanyakazi wa kwanza walitarajia zaidi ya aliyewaahidi. Kwa sababu walitarajia atawatolea zaidi ya senti, walimlaumu. Usiwe na matarajio makali kwa vitu ambavyo Mungu hajawaahidi katika Biblia, hata kama unahisi kwamba Mungu amevekuawazi kwa Roho wake. Ni bora kuwa na moyo mnyenyekevu, wazi kwa Mungu, familia, na ndugu wa imani.

Ushirikiano

Ushirikiano na watu wa Mungu ni hatua nyingine muhimu katika njia ya kukamilika. Usijitegemee, bali jiunge na watu wa Mungu.

“Basi wale waliopokea neno kwa moyo mmoja walibatizwa; na siku hiyo takriban roho elfu tatu zilikuzwa. 42 Na waliendelea kwaza katika mafundisho ya mitume, na katika ushirikiano, na katika kuvunja mkate, na katika sala” (Matendo 2:41).

Inaweza kuwa rahisi kuanguka kwenye mtego wa kuhisi kwamba wewe ni tofauti na kila mtu na haufai. Kumbuka kwamba kila mtu ni wa kipekee, na pamoja tunaunda mwili wa Kristo. Wewe ni mwanachama muhimu na una vipaji na uwezo vinavyohitajika katika ushirika wako wa karibu. Tumia muda na watu na tafuta njia za kuwa baraka na kuwasaidia wengine.

Utambulisho

Kubali utambulisho wako. Unaweza kujiuliza, mimi ni nani? Ninaendaje? Hii inaweza kuwa ngumu hasa ikiwa una tamaa kubwa ya kuolewa lakini haupo. Unaweza kuona wengine wakifanikia kile unachokitamani kuwa.

Unaweza kujiuliza, kuna nini kibaya nami kwamba mimi si mume au mke? Hili ni fikra isiyo sahihi. Ukweli ni kwamba kuna watu wengi walioolewa ambao wako katika hali mbaya zaidi kuliko wewe. Kuwa wazi wakati wale wako karibu nao wanapokuwa na mawazo kuhusu mabadiliko unayoweza na unayopaswa kufanya maishani mwako, lakini usijitime kama haupo vizuri vya kutosha na kwamba wengine hawakukubali. Waefeso sura ya 1 inasema kwamba umechaguliwa na Mungu kusafishwa dhambi zako kupitia damu ya Yesu na kutanganywa kuwa mtoto Wake. Umekubaliwa na Mungu, na uko “kwa utukufu wa heshima yake!”

Kusudi

Hatua ya mwisho ninayoandika kuhusu ni kuhusu kusudi. Nini kitu kimoja unachopenda kufanya ambacho ni baraka kwa kanisa au Ufalme? Mungu ana kusudi kwako kutimizwa. Uwe sehemu ya ufalme Wake ambayo unaweza kuwekeza muda na nguvu. Mungu ametuita kila mmoja wetu kuwa mtumishi, kufuata nyayo za Bwana wetu Yesu. Inaweza kuwa rahisi kama kumtoa glasi ya maji baridi kwa jina la Yesu. Hakuna kazi ndogo sana au ya kawaida kuwa sehemu ya ufalme Wake. Kuwa tayari. Kuwa na moyo wa mtumishi. Ukiona hitaji, toa mkono wa msaada au sikio la kusikiliza.

“Msione kila mtu vitu vyake mwenyewe pekee, bali kila mtu pia kwa mambo ya wengine. 5 Nafasi hii iwe ndani yenu ambayo pia ilikuwa ndani ya Kristo Yesu: 6 Ambaye akiwa katika umbo la Mungu, hakuwahesabu kuwa nyakuwi kuwa sawa na Mungu; 7 Lakini alifanya nafsi yake kuwa haina sifa, akachukua umbo wa mtumishi, na akafanywa kuwa katika mfano wa wanadamu:” (Wafilipi 2:4) Mimi na mke wangu hivi karibuni tulisherehekea kumbukumbu yetu ya ndoa ya tatu. Nilikuwa na umri wa miaka 38 na Jena 29 tulipoonana ndoa. Machipukizi ya msimu uliopita tulibarikiwa na msichana mdogo mrembo, Gianna. Ningependa kusema kwamba tulitenda kila wakati yale niliyoyaandika katika makala hii, lakini sisi ni wanadamu na tulikosea wakati mwingine. Lakini tunaweza wote kusema kwa uzoefu kwamba mambo niliyoyaandika ni halisi na ya kweli. Kuna njia ya furaha na ukamilifu kama mtu asiyeoa. Jena alifuata taaluma ya kuwachukua wajawazito na alijinyima mengi kumtumikia mama na watoto. Daima alikuwa tayari kuacha yale anayofanya au kuruka kitandani katikati ya usiku kwenda kutumikia. Mimi nilifanya tafiti nyingi za Biblia na pia safari za Mashariki ya Kati kusoma Biblia kwa kipimo tofauti. Mungu amenijalia neema ya kutembelea sehemu ambazo watu wazuri wachache wamekuwa. Nimeweza kuona mahali watu wengi wa Biblia waliishi na kutembea, wakiwemo Nuhu, Abrahamu, Isaka, Yakobo, Musa, Daudi, na, bora zaidi kabisa, Yesu. Watu hawa waliwaacha ushuhuda wa imani na utiifu. Tufuatie!

“Kwa hiyo tukiona kwamba tumezungukwa na wingu kubwa wa mashahidi, tuweke kando kila uzito, na dhambi inayotushika kwa urahisi, na tukimbie kwa uvumilivu mbio zilizo mbele yetu, 2 Tukitazama kwa makini Yesu muumba na mkamilishaji wa imani yetu; ambaye kwa furaha iliyokuwa mbele yake alistahimili msalaba, akadharau aibu, na ameketi mkononi mwa taji la Mungu. 3 Kwa maana mzingatie yeye aliyependwa vivyo hivyo na wana dhambi dhidi yake, ili msichoke na kulemewa kwa nia . . . (Waebrania 12:1-3).

“Kwa hiyo ininyanyeni mikono iliyoteleza, na jino mchanga; 13 Na fafanua njia za miguuni mwenu, ili huyo mwenye ulemavu asipotee; bali aoachane na hilo apone. 14 Tafuteni amani na watu wote, na utakatifu, bila yake hakuna mtu ataemuona Bwana: 15 Mwangalieni kwa bidii kwamba mtu yeyote asifikie kutokuwa na neema ya Mungu; ili asije mzizi wowote wa uchungu ukikatika na kuwachafua wengi . . . (Waebrania 12:12-15)

“Kwa hiyo sisi tukipokea ufalme usioweza kuhamishwa, tuwe na neema, kupitia ambayo tumpokee Mungu kwa kufaulu kwa heshima na woga wa kimungu” (Waebrania 12;28).

I doubt that there is a soul alive that has not been offended at one time or another. The persistent weeds of evil influence seem to sprout at every corner, testing the best of blooming relationships. The more communication tools we possess, the more miscommunication we seem to encounter, and people are offended. Ministers of the Gospel today are expected to be soft and effeminate lest they offend their listeners. While we certainly must meet people where they are and seek not to offend them, the bane of the modern church is not the bold and offensive minister.

I wish to give no license to hardhearted preachers who are void of tenderness and tears. Woe be unto the dry-eyed prophets who wield the sword of the Lord without an ounce of consideration that there are real people between the ears that they are chopping off in the process. Yet, it seems that there is an epidemic of our day that has surpassed the bubonic plague, outstripped the damage of polio, and makes our modern cancer appear like a minor inconvenience. I speak to the outbreak of the millions of offended hearts that are arising from the rubbish of the innumerable hordes of broken and strained relationships about us on every hand. Jesus mentioned that one of the signs of the end times is that “then shall many be offended . . . and shall hate one another” (Matthew 24:10). Divorce-riddled homes have risen to an all-time high, producing a generation of immense mistrust and pain. Couples will deem themselves as incompatible and separate at the slightest offense. Christians will spend years outside a church setting because they have been offended by fellow believers.

Many will automatically side with the offended party, assuming them to be a victim. Many times they are. “Woe unto the world because of offences!” (Matthew 18:7) But the equation changes when we consider that the sinless Christ offended many. He told His disciples that they must eat His flesh and many left Him. He informed the inner 12 that had stuck with Him, “All ye shall be offended because of me this night” (Mark 14:27). The Pharisees were offended when Christ exposed their vain worship, and Jesus offended His own countrymen simply by doing good. The Greek word is skandalízō meaning “to scandalize”.1 In Hebrew, it means “a stumbling block”. The problem is that many today will stumble over the slightest obstruction in their path and the molehill becomes a mountain.

“Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them” (Psalm 119:165). What shall we say then to this passage? Here are people who have learned how to walk upon the rocky path of life without going down every time a discomfiting obstacle arises before them. We wish to heap no condemnation upon the sensitive soul, but the word sensitive is not in the Bible. The closest word we can find there is sensual, which is very similar in its roots and means natural. Christ described these plants as having “not root in himself, but dureth for a while: for when tribulation or persecution ariseth because of the word, by and by he is offended” (Matthew 13:20-21). It is so easy and very natural to feel sorry for the offended. They carry a tremendous sob story, and they usually share it in tears. “In many things, we offend all” (James 3:2). No one is as sinless in their offending as Christ, so there is usually an element of truth poured out against the offender. It seems to me that we all would be much further down the road if we would withhold some of our sympathy for the offended and spend our energies teaching them how to walk upright on the path of life despite the jagged and copious stumbling stones that greet us daily upon our journey. We will learn to live life unoffended when we learn to . . .

Walk Worthy

“I therefore, the prisoner of the Lord, beseech you that ye walk worthy of the vocation wherewith ye are called, with all lowliness and meekness, with longsuffering, forbearing one another in love” (Ephesians 4:1-2). To walk worthy, as Paul describes it here, is to walk in humility. “Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall” (Proverbs 16:18). The more pride-laden our vessel, the more apt we are to be offended. The more honestly we appraise our worth, the less offended we shall be when derided. More humble equals less stumble. When we are accused of a wrong, it always hurts. Jesus says that we should be happy when people say all manner of evil against us falsely. While such a demeaning wound may fester under our skin, there is a condition that is far worse. That is when people say all evil against us truly. Many accusations against us carry a certain percentage of truth in them. It is this portion that the Lord would have us to reckon with, rather than decrying the overstatement. While these falsities levied against us may raise our ire, they are not the reason we stumble and walk around with consequential bruises. Offense arises when the opinion of another doesn't measure up to the extent we tout ourselves.

“Cast ye up, cast ye up, prepare the way, take up the stumbling block out of the way of my people. For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy; I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones” (Isaiah 57:14-15). Here, Isaiah instructs us to remove the stumbling block but makes no mention of the offender. The antidote is to be of a contrite and humble spirit. We will never be able to exterminate every avenue of offense. But if reckoned correctly, there is no offense that shall ever be able to divert us from the promise, “they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint” (Isaiah 40:31). It is predominantly our pride which stands in the way of our successful journey, rather than ill-treatment.

Walk In Love

“And walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us, and hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweet smelling savour. But fornication, and all uncleanness, or covetousness, let it not be once named among you, as becometh saints; neither filthiness, nor foolish talking, nor jesting . . .” (Ephesians 5:2-4). It takes no scholar to observe the stumblings of a selfish fool. This selfish ambition to obtain friends, wealth, and affluence is guaranteed to bring a man flat on his nose at some time or another. The trail of sins mentioned here are all following in tow to the gratifying of self. King Ahasuerus counseled of Haman on how to honor a worthy man. Haman’s narcissistic mind immediately brooded, “To whom would the king delight to do honour more than to myself?” (Esther 6:6). God had other plans thus the man who was so offended by Mordecai was hung upon the gallows of his own creation. Selfish souls can point to a thousand and one reasons why they are not attaining their aspirations. Somebody wronged them. An unfortunate turn of events derailed them. But it was not Mordecai, Esther, nor even Ahasuerus that brought Haman stumbling to his bitter end. It was his own refusal to walk in love and to sacrifice himself for others that wrought the malignant demise in his soul.

Walk as Children of Light

“Walk as children of light . . . proving what is acceptable unto the Lord. And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove them” (Ephesians 5:8-11). Our innate passions contain the third rock of offense. There may be things that we believe are acceptable to our Lord, which are not. There are those who have “itching ears; and they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables” (2 Timothy 4:3-4). This may affect those with the most noble intentions and firm beliefs. Christ forewarned His disciples that they would be put out of the synagogues so that when it happened, they “should not be offended” (John 16:1-4).

John the Baptist was a burning and a shining light and no prophet born of women had risen greater. He walked worthy of his calling, baptized the Lord, and rebuked the Pharisees. He walked in love, and multitudes “were willing for a season to rejoice in his light” (John 5:35). Yet the day came when he sent his disciples to ask Jesus: Art thou he that should come? Or look we for another? To which Jesus replied, “Go your way, and tell John what things ye have seen and heard; how that the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, to the poor the gospel is preached ... and blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me” (Luke 7:20-23). Christ's response would indicate that this apparently did not fully fit the aspirations of what John had in mind, and he was struggling to accept it. Like his Old Testament counterpart, Elijah, these like passions provided the fodder for the flames of discouragement. It seemed to John that evil had enveloped the nation and God wasn't doing His part.

We may mean well, but our own passionate feelings are not a good gauge of proving what is acceptable unto the Lord. Phaltiel was a dear soul who fell into such deceit. He had been given Michal by King Saul himself. The princess was no doubt a delicate and pleasing prize. David had evidently valued her so, for he risked his life and doubled the dowry with two hundred Philistine foreskins to secure her hand in marriage. But Phaltiel thought nothing of that, relishing his own good fortune and so enjoyed her company for years. Though this arrangement may have been socially acceptable at the time, no man has the right to receive what another has no right to give. The day came when “they sent, and took her from her husband, even from Phaltiel the son of Laish. And her husband went with her along weeping behind her” (2 Samuel 3:15-16). We know very little of Phaltiel, but if we dismiss ourselves from his emotional avalanche, we must declare him faulty. We dare not let our compassionate heart turn toward him or toward anyone who is offended when asked to separate from works of darkness. When these passionate feelings are allowed to rule, offense is the inevitable result. “For what glory is it, if, when ye be buffeted for your faults, ye shall take it patiently? But if, when ye do well, and suffer for it, ye take it patiently, this is acceptable with God” (1 Peter 2:20) . . .

Walk Circumspectly

“See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise” (Ephesians 5:15). “Be not children in understanding: howbeit in malice be ye children, but in understanding be men” (1 Corinthians 14:20). Herein we must honestly acknowledge that ignorance is not bliss. To enter the narrow gate may require a broad mind. Not so broad to allow sin, but broad enough to allow God. Circumspect is a compound word formed from the Latin words circum (around) and spectare (to behold). The one-dimensional soul will spend his days being offended, for he cannot see from the viewpoint of any but his own. There are over a dozen solid scriptures warning us against doing what is right in our own eyes. We must learn to honestly consider the counsel and wisdom of others lest we fall into condemnation.

In her early years, Michal loved David with deep and fervent loyalty but later fell prey to rash judgment. “As the ark of the LORD came into the city of David, Michal, Saul's daughter looked through a window, and saw king David leaping and dancing before the LORD; and she despised him in her heart” (2 Samuel 6:16). As Michal viewed the scene from her upper vantage, there were two things evident. First, David was exuberantly thankful, and his joy knew no bounds. This is first love, “for whether we be beside ourselves, it is to God” (2 Corinthians 5:13). Second, during David's ecstatic dancing in his loin cloth, his discretion elapsed, and his flesh became a bit public. This would require great circumspection to view from another portal, and Michal will have none of it. Upon his entrance to bless his house, David was met with a blast of pent-up bigotry from his offended and sarcastic wife. While the accusation carried a dimension of truth, to cling to it as supreme was shameful prejudice. God had no sympathy for it and “therefore Michal the daughter of Saul had no child unto the day of her death” (2 Samuel 6:23). Many a good woman has judged her man from her singular corner and parched the soil of the home with the same arid judgment. This narrow-mindedness will never be fruitful no matter how blatant the accusation. There is a correct way to express concern, but the outpouring of biased judgment will turn a celestial oasis into a barren wasteland in a prompt fashion.

“A brother offended is harder to be won than a strong city: and their contentions are like the bars of a castle” (Proverbs 18:19). So it is with a sister, husband, wife, friend, etc. While causes for offense abound on every side, does Christ desire us to be offended? Will He salute our sour and shriveled soul? Perhaps He gave us this test so that we may have root within ourselves, “that no man should be moved by these afflictions” (1 Thessalonians 3:3). While we may not be able to control our feelings during times of inward pain, we each can choose a redemptive path and walk in the Spirit. It is a choice to broadcast grievances, nurse hurts, withdraw from the offender, and decline to believe all things. Like the brother offended, these contentions serve to lock the soul like the bars of a castle. But who holds the power for release?
