Nina shaka kama kuna nafsi hai ambayo hajawahi kuchukizwa mara moja au nyingine. Magugu ya kuendelea ya ushawishi wa uovu yanaonekana kuchipuka kila kona, yakijaribu uhusiano bora zaidi. Kadiri tunavyokuwa na zana nyingi za mawasiliano, ndivyo tunavyokutana na hitilafu nyingi za mawasiliano, na watu wanachukizwa. Wao wa Injili leo wanatarajiwa kuwa laini na wa kifalme ili wasiwachukize wasikilizaji wao. Ingawa bila shaka lazima tukutane na watu pale walipo na kutolenga kuwachukiza, janga la kanisa la kisasa si mchungaji jasiri anayewachukiza watu.

Nisiwekitoleo kwa wachungaji wenye mioyo migumu ambao hawana huruma wala machozi. Je, mbaya iwe kwa manabii wenye macho yasiyo na unyevu ambao wanatumia upanga wa Bwana bila wazo hata kidogo kwamba kuna watu halisi kati ya masikio ambao wanavamiwa kwa kukatwa kwa njia hiyo. Hata hivyo, inaonekana kuna janga la siku zetu ambalo limezidi mafua, likazidi madhara ya polio, na kuifanya saratani yetu ya kisasa ionekane kama usumbufu mdogo. Ninazungumzia mlipuko wa mamilioni ya mioyo iliyochukizwa inayotokana na takataka za majeshi mengi ya uhusiano uliovunwa na kupasuka karibu nasi kila upande. Yesu alitaja kwamba moja ya dalili za nyakati za mwisho ni kwamba “kisha watu wengi watadanganyika ... na watakuwa na chuki kwa kila mmoja” (Mathayo 24:10). Nyumba zilizojaa talaka zimefikia kiwango cha juu kabisa, zikizalisha kizazi cha kutoamini sana na maumivu. Wapenzi watajiona hawana sifa za kuendana na kutengana kwa kosa dogo kabisa. Wakristo watatumia miaka nje ya jamaa ya kanisa kwa sababu wamechukizwa na waumini wenzake.

Wengi watampendelea upande wa aliyekuwa amechukizwa, wakidhani yeye ndiye mhanga. Mara nyingi ni yeye. “Je, mbaya iwe kwa ulimwengu kwa ajili ya dhambi!” (Mathayo 18:7) Lakini hesabu hubadilika tunapozingatia kwamba Kristo asiye na dhambi aliwachukiza wengi. Aliwaambia wanafunzi wake kwamba lazima wakule nyama yake na wengi walimuacha. Aliwaambia wale wa ndani kumi na wawili waliomwangalia, “Nyinyi nyote mtaanguka kwasababu yangu usiku huu” (Marko 14:27). Mafarisayo walichukizwa wakati Kristo alifunua ibada yao ya ubinafsi, na Yesu aliwachukiza hata watu wa mji wake kwa kufanya wema tu. Neno la Kigriki ni skandalízō lenye maana ya “kusababisha skandali”.1 Katika Kiebrania, linamaanisha “kinachosababisha kukanyaga” — kikwazo cha kukanyaga. Shida ni kwamba wengi leo watakanyaga juu ya kizuizi kidogo kabisa katika njia yao na mfereji mdogo ukawa mlima.

“Amani kuu watakayo wapenda sheria yako: wala wala watadhalilishwa” (Zaburi 119:165). Tuseme nini basi kuhusu kifungu hiki? Hapa kuna watu waliyejifunza jinsi ya kutembea juu ya njia ya mwamba ya maisha bila kuanguka kila wakati kimbadiliko kinapojitokeza mbele yao. Hatutaki kuweka hukumu kwa nafsi nyeti, lakini neno nyeti halipo katika Biblia. Neno karibu tunaloweza kupata humo ni la kihisia (sensual), ambalo linadumu mizizi yake na lina maana ya asili. Kristo alielezea mimea hii kuwa haina mzizi ndani yake, “bali husema kwa muda, kwa maana tafrani au mateso yakitokea kwa ajili ya neno, mara tu anachukizwa” (Mathayo 13:20-21). Ni rahisi na ni asili kumwonea huruma aliyekuwa amechukizwa. Wana hadithi kubwa ya kuomboleza, na kawaida wanaishirikisha kwa machozi. “Katika mambo mengi, sisi sote tunajichukulia kosa” (Yakobo 3:2). Hakuna mtu mtakatifu katika kunyima haki kama Kristo, hivyo kawaida kuna kipengele cha kweli kinachomwaga lawama dhidi ya mwenye kosa. Kwangu inaonekana tusingeendelea mbele kama sivyo tukipunguza baadhi ya huruma zetu kwa waliochukizwa na kutumia nguvu zetu kufundisha jinsi ya kutembea wima katika njia ya maisha licha ya mawe mengi na makali yanayotuliza kila siku katika safari yetu. Tutaweza kuishi bila kuchukizwa tunapojifunza ku...

Tembea Ustahili

“Basi mimi, mfungwa wa Bwana, nawaomba mtatembee kwa ustahili wa wito nanyi ulioitwa, kwa unyenyekevu wote na upole, kwa uvumilivu, mnavumiliana kwa upendo” (Ephesians 4:1-2). Kutembea kwa ustahili, kama Paulo anavyoelezea hapa, ni kutembea kwa unyenyekevu. “Kiburi huenda mbele ya uharibifu, na mtukufu wa roho mbele ya kuanguka” (Methali 16:18). Kadiri chombo chetu chenye kiburi kilivyo, ndivyo tunavyoweza kuchukizwa zaidi. Kadiri tunavyojiangalia kwa uwazi zaidi, ndivyo tutakavyokuwa wachache wa kuchukizwa tunapokatiliwa. Unyenyekevu zaidi = kukanyaga kidogo. Tunapokosolewa kwa kosa, mara zote inachoma. Yesu anasema kuwa tunapaswa kufurahi wanaposema kila aina ya uovu dhidi yetu kwa uongo. Ingawa jeraha la kudhalilisha linaweza kuvimba chini ya ngozi yetu, kuna hali mbaya zaidi. Hiyo ni wakati watu wanaposema uovu wote dhidi yetu ukweli. Madai mengi dhidi yetu yana asilimia fulani ya kweli ndani yao. Ni sehemu hii ambayo Bwana angependa tuzingatie, badala ya kulaani kupitishwa kupita kiasi. Wakati uongozi uliopelekwa kwetu unaweza kuchochea hasira yetu, siyo sababu tunaanguka na kutembea tukiwa na majeraha makubwa. Uchokozi unatokea wakati maoni ya mwingine hayalingani na kiwango tunajidanganya sisi wenyewe.

“Piga, piga, andaa njia, toa kizingiti katika njia ya watu wangu. Kwa maana hivi anasema Aliye Juu na Aliye Mtakatifu mwenye kuishi milele, jina lake ni Mtakatifu; mimi nakuwepo mahali pa juu na takatifu, nami naye ambaye ana roho ya kugaluliwa na unyenyekevu, nikuinue roho ya walio wanyenyekevu, na nikuboreshe mioyo ya walioghalalika” (Isaiah 57:14-15). Hapa, Isaya anatupatia maagizo ya kuondoa kizingiti lakini hakusema chochote kuhusu mwenye kumuudhi. Tiba ni kuwa na roho ya kugaluliwa na unyenyekevu. Hatutawahi kuweza kuua kila njia ya kuchukizwa. Lakini iwapo tutayafanyia hesabu kwa usahihi, hakuna udhalilisho utakaoweza kututenganisha na ahadi, “watainuka kwa mapacha kama tai; watakimbia wala wasichoke; watatembea wala wasikate tamaa” (Isaiah 40:31). Ni hasa kiburi chetu ndicho kinachoshikilia safari yetu yenye mafanikio, badala ya kutendewa vibaya.

Tembea kwa Upendo

“Na tembeni kwa upendo, kama Kristo alivyotupenda, naye akajitoa kwa ajili yetu kuwa sadaka na dhabihu kwa Mungu kuwa harufu ya kupendeza. Lakini uzinzi, na uchafu wote, au tamaa za pesa, asikuzungumzwe hata mara moja miongoni mwenu, kama inafaa watakatifu; wala uchafu, wala maneno ya kijinga, wala ucheshi ...” (Ephesians 5:2-4). Haina haja ya mtaalamu kutambua mapungufu ya mpumbavu mwenye ubinafsi. Ubahati wa kutaka kupata marafiki, mali, na ustawi ni uhakika wa kumweka mtu uso chini kwa wakati fulani. Lafu ya dhambi zilizotajwa hapa zinafuata kutimizwa kwa nafsi yake. Mfalme Ahasuweli alimuikubali Haman jinsi ya kumheshimu mtu mwenye sifa. Akili ya kibinafsi ya Haman mara moja ilifikiria, “Kwa nani mfalme angefurahia kumheshimu zaidi kuliko mimi?” (Esther 6:6). Mungu alikuwa na mipango mingine; hivyo mtu aliyechukizwa sana na Mordekai aliteswa kwa mti wa kifo aliyojiunda mwenyewe. Nafsi zenye ubinafsi zinaweza kutaja sababu elfu moja na moja kwanini hawawezi kufikia matarajio yao. Mtu alimkosea. Mabadiliko mabaya ya matukio yaliwatatiza. Lakini si Mordekai, Esther, wala hata Ahasuweli aliyeleta Haman kuanguka hadi mwisho wake mchungu. Ilikuwa kukataa kwake kutembea kwa upendo na kujitoa kwa wengine ambayo ilisababisha kifo kibaya ndani ya nafsi yake.

Tembea kama Watoto wa Mwangaza

“Tembeni kama watoto wa nuru ... mkitafuta yale yanayofaa kwa Bwana. Msiwe na mshikamano na kazi zisizozaa za giza, bali zizihoji” (Ephesians 5:8-11). Tamaa zetu za asili zina kizingiti cha tatu cha kuchukizwa. Kuna mambo ambayo tunaamini yanamkubalika Bwana wetu, ambayo siyo. Kuna wale wenye “masikio yanayotaka kuumwa; wamegeuka masikio yao mbali na ukweli, na watageuka kwa hadithi” (2 Timothy 4:3-4). Hii inaweza kumgusa hata aliyekuwa na nia njema na imani thabiti. Kristo alionya wanafunzi wake kwamba watatolewa kwa masinagogi ili wakati kitendawili hicho kitendeke, wasiwe wachukizwe (John 16:1-4).

Yohana Mbatizaji alikuwa mwanga unaowaka na kuangaza, na hakuna nabii aliyezaliwa wa wanawake aliyekuwa mkuu kuliko yeye. Alitembea kwa ustahili wa wito wake, akabatiza Bwana, na akamkemea Mafarisayo. Alitembea kwa upendo, na maelfu “walikuwa wakitamani kwa wakati kufurahia mwangaza wake” (John 5:35). Hata hivyo siku ilifika alipomtuma wanafunzi wake kumuuliza Yesu: Je, wewe ndiye atakayekuja? Au tazamia mwingine? Yesu akawajibu, “Nendeni, mkamwambieni Yohana mliyoona na kusikia: jinsi vipofu wanavyoona, wapotovu wanavyotembea, waziofukuzwa wanavyosafishwa, viziwi wanavyosikia, wafu wanavyofufuka, habari njema inavyotangazwa kwa maskini ... na amefariki ni yule ambaye hatachukizwa kwangu” (Luke 7:20-23). Jibu la Kristo lingekuwa linaonyesha kwamba jambo hili halikukidhi kabisa matarajio ya Yohana, na alikuwa akipigana kukubali. Kama mwenzake wa Agano la Kale, Eliya, tamaa kama hizi zilikuwa mzizi wa miiba ya moyo. Kwa Yohana ilionekana kama uovu ulikuwa umemzimia taifa na Mungu hajafanya sehemu yake.

Tunaweza kuwa na nia njema, lakini hisia zetu mwenyewe zenye mwitikio si kipimo kizuri cha kuthibitisha nini kinakubalika kwa Bwana. Paltieli alikuwa nafsi mpendwa aliyeanguka katika udanganyifu huo. Alimpatwa Michali kwa mfalme Sauli mwenyewe. Malkia huyo bila shaka alikuwa zawadi ya kupendeza. Daudi alikuwa anamthamini, kwa maana alitilia hatari maisha yake na kuongezea morgongo kwa kanuni za mafungu mia mbili za Waafilisti ili kupata mkono wake kwa ndoa. Lakini Paltieli hakujali hayo, akifurahia bahati yake mwenyewe na hivyo kufurahia kampeni yake kwa miaka mingi. Ingawa mpangilio huo pengine ulikubalika kijamii wakati huo, hakuna mtu anayestahili kupokea kile ambacho mwingine hana haki ya kutoa. Siku ilikuja “wakamtuma, na wakamchukua kwa mumewe, hata kutoka kwa Paltieli mwana wa Laishi. Na mumewe alifuata naye akiwa analia nyuma yake” (2 Samuel 3:15-16). Hatuna habari nyingi kuhusu Paltieli, lakini tukijiondoa kutoka kwa mteremko wa hisia zake, lazima tumtaja mwenye dosari. Hatupaswi kumruhusu moyo wetu wa huruma kumgeukia yeye au mtu yeyote aliyekuwa amechukizwa anapohitajika kutengwa kutoka kwa kazi za giza. Wakati hisia hizi zinaporuhusiwa kutawala, kuchukizwa ndiko matokeo yasiyoweza kuepukika. “Kwa maana ni heri ikiwa, mkiugandamana kwa makosa yenu, mkatambulia kwa subira? Lakini ikiwa, mkiyetenda mema na mkateswa kwa ajili yake, mkatambulia kwa subira, hii ni kukubalika kwa Mungu” (1 Peter 2:20) ...

Tembea kwa Kuweka Tahadhari

“Basi angalieni jinsi mnavyotembea kwa tahadhari, siyo kama wajinga bali kama wenye busara” (Ephesians 5:15). “Msimwagee mtoto kwa akili: ingawa kwa ubaya muwe watoto, lakini kwa akili muwe watu” (1 Corinthians 14:20). Hapa lazima tukubali kwa uaminifu kwamba ujinga si furaha. Kuingia katika lango nyembamba kunaweza kuhitaji akili pana. Sio pana mno kuruhusu dhambi, bali pana vya kutosha kumruhusu Mungu. Tahadhari ni neno la mseto lililotokana na maneno ya Kilatini circum (kuzunguka) na spectare (kutazama). Nafsi yenye upande mmoja itatumia siku zake kuchukizwa, kwa sababu haitiwezi kuona kutoka mtazamo wa yeyote ila wake mwenyewe. Kuna maandiko zaidi ya kumi ya moyo yasiyopindukia yanayotuwahadharisha dhidi ya kufanya kile tunachokiona kuwa sawa machoni mwetu. Lazima tujifunze kuzingatia kwa uaminifu ushauri na busara za wengine ili tusijengenewe hukumu.

Katika miaka yake ya awali, Michali alipenda Daudi kwa uaminifu wa kina na shauku lakini baadaye akamwangukia hukumu ya haraka. “Wakati safina ya Bwana ilipopofuka katika mji wa Daudi, Michali, binti wa Sauli alitazama kupitia dirisha, akamuona mfalme Daudi akikimbizwa na kucheza mbele za Bwana; naye alimchukia moyoni mwake” (2 Samuel 6:16). Michali alipokuwa akiangalia tukio hilo kutoka sehemu yake ya juu, mambo mawili yalionekana wazi. Kwanza, Daudi alikuwa mtegemeo wa shukrani, na furaha yake haina mipaka. Hii ni upendo wa kwanza, “kwa maana ikiwa sisi ni wajinga, ni kwa ajili ya Mungu” (2 Corinthians 5:13). Pili, wakati Daudi alikuwa akicheza kwa furaha akiwa amevaa nguo za ndani, busara yake ilipotea, na mwili wake ukawa wazi kidogo. Hii ingehitaji tahadhari kubwa kuangalia kutoka dirisha lingine, na Michali hakupenda kabisa. Alipoingia kwake kuibariki nyumba yake, Daudi alikutana na shambulio la chuki zilizofichwa kutoka kwa mke wake aliyekuwa amechukizwa na matusi. Ingawa kosa lilikuwa na kipengele cha kweli, kushikilia hilo kama la juu kabisa ilikuwa aibu ya kupendelea upande mmoja. Mungu hakumchukulia huruma, na “hivyo Michali binti wa Sauli hakuwa na mtoto hadi siku ya kifo chake” (2 Samuel 6:23). Mwanamke mzuri mwingi amemhukumu mume wake kutoka kona yake ya pekee na kukaukisha udongo wa nyumba kwa hukumu hiyo kavu. Ufikiri huo wa upande mmoja hautazaa matunda hata tu kosa likiwa wazi. Kuna njia sahihi ya kuonyesha wasi wasi, lakini kumwaga hukumu ya upande mmoja kutageuza oasi ya mbinguni kuwa jangwani kwa haraka.

“Kaka aliyechukizwa ni mgumu kushinda kuliko mji wenye nguvu: na mabishano yao ni kama nanga za ngome” (Methali 18:19). Hivyo ndivyo ilivyo kwa dada, mume, mke, rafiki, n.k. Ingawa sababu za kuchukizwa zipo kila upande, je, Kristo anataka tuwe wachukizwe? Je, atampongeza nafsi yetu iliyochoka na kuharibika? Labda alitupa mtihani huu ili tuwe na mzizi ndani yetu, “kwa kuwa mtu asizungushwe na mateso haya” (1 Thessalonians 3:3). Ingawa hatuwezi kudhibiti hisia zetu wakati wa maumivu ya ndani, kila mmoja wetu anaweza kuchagua njia ya ukombozi na kutembea kwa Roho. Ni uamuzi kutangaza malalamiko, kulea maumivu, kujiondoa kwa mtenda makosa, na kukataa kuamini mambo yote. Kama kaka aliyekuwa amechukizwa, mabishano haya yanatumikia kufunga nafsi kama nanga za ngome. Lakini nani anashikilia nguvu ya kuachilia?

Can I have a fulfilled heart if there is a vision, a hope, and or a dream in my life that lies barren and unrealized? Must I go through life carrying a cross of pain and loneliness while God answers the prayers of my friends and gives them the desires of their hearts? Is something wrong with me? Is my faith too weak? Have I not prayed enough, surrendered enough, been obedient enough? What is life all about? Why don’t I have peace and joy? Does God have a plan and a purpose for me?

“Thou wilt shew me the path of life: in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore” (Psalms 16:11).

“And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper” (Psalms 1:3).

God has a path provided for each of us that will lead to a fulfilled heart. In God’s presence, there is fullness of joy! God’s desire is that your heart would be like a riverside tree, filled with life, health, strength, and fruit. He desires that you experience grace, joy, and peace, in your everyday life. God wants to fill your heart with his desires and purposes. He longs for you to seek after his will and plan. If you walk on his pathway, you will be filled with blessing and grace. This does not mean that every desire that you may have comes to pass (I don’t think that will ever happen for anyone in this life) but rather that your heart is full of the blessings of God. Your heart does not need to feel like a desert, the Water of Life can fill it.

“But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14).

Where does Fulfillment Begin?

Fulfillment starts in your relationship with God. Does He feel cold and distant to you, or do you find joy and peace in praying and walking with him? Do you know that your sins are forgiven and that you are accepted as His child? Do you obey God with a willing heart or are there areas in your life where you resist his will as revealed in the Bible? Walking in the love and grace of God is the most important thing you can do in life. This is the first step on the pathway to a fulfilled heart.

If you are struggling in your relationship with God and are not sure of his love, forgiveness, and acceptance, here are some directions from the Bible for you.

“But the righteousness which is of faith speaketh on this wise, Say not in thine heart, Who shall ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down from above:) 7 Or, Who shall descend into the deep? (that is, to bring up Christ again from the dead.) 8 But what saith it? The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach; 9 That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved. 10 For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation” (Romans 10:6-10).

You should never think that Christ is in some unapproachable place, and unavailable to you. Christ is made known to you by the Bible, his Holy Spirit, and by his creation. Unbelief, sin, disobedience, and unforgiveness to others can keep you from experiencing his love and grace. Opening your heart to Him by faith, believing in your heart, and confessing with your mouth the Lord Jesus, will restore your relationship with God. He will wash away your sin and receive you as his child. Christ came to this earth to reconcile us to God. He paid the price of our sin and guilt. We can receive his gift of salvation through faith and repentance. Faith is simply hearing the Word of God and receiving it into our hearts.

As we receive the Word of God into our hearts, it enables us to be obedient to his will. We choose to believe all that God has spoken to us in the Bible. We let go of all our doubts and embrace His Word. Repentance is turning away from our own selfish will and our sinful ways and choosing to obey God and his Word. In 1 John 1:9 God has said that if we confess our sins, He will forgive us. Do you truly believe this? Is it hard for you to accept that he will forgive you? It is impossible for God to lie, therefore his Word and promises can always be trusted.

Practical ways to walk with God

“There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit” (Romans 8:1).

There are spiritual prerequisites needed to walk with God. If we don’t have a right heart, these practical things won’t actually help us walk with God. It will only be an empty activity with no real meaning and little benefit.

With our hearts full of faith and love we need to believe everything in the Bible. We need to believe all its history, everything it says about the man, Jesus, all the prophecies, and all the direction God gives us in the Word.

We also need a surrendered heart and choose to follow and obey God in everything. There is no area in which we choose to neglect or disobey. We need to have confessed our sins and be born again by the Spirit of God.

Pray. For yourself, God’s kingdom, your family, the church, neighbors, widows and widowers, orphans, missionaries, governments, and the sick. Pray for people who have lost loved ones, hungry people, people in prison, and people who need salvation. Pray for God to send workers into the vineyard.

Study the Word. Memorize it and read it to others. Discuss it.

Sing praises to God! God has been so merciful to you. Rejoice in your salvation!

“And that the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy; as it is written, For this cause I will confess to thee among the Gentiles, and sing unto thy name. 10 And again he saith, Rejoice, ye Gentiles, with his people. 11 And again, Praise the Lord, all ye Gentiles; and laud him, all ye people” (Romans 15:9).

Contentment

Another big step in the pathway to a fulfilled heart is contentment. You can never be fulfilled if you aren’t content in knowing that you are in the will of God.

“Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee. 6 So that we may boldly say, The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me” (Hebrews 13:5).

What is covetousness? My definition of covetousness is having a strong desire for something that is outside of God’s will for me right now. Normally, covetousness will drive you to violate scripture and God’s will, to try to obtain the thing you have a desire for. For instance, if you are covetous of money, you will tend to do unethical things or neglect to follow the direction in the Bible in your pursuit of money. You may cheat, steal, scam, overcharge, or become a workaholic and neglect God, family, church, or the needy.

God has given us desires, and it is a good thing to pursue them if our heart is surrendered, seeking God’s will and pursuing it according to the direction given in the Bible. Seek to move forward, but never force your own will. Be open to the people that God has put in your life for direction.

You may be at the age when your friends are getting married. You also desire to get married, but all the doors slam shut in your face. It seems like God reveals his will to others but not you. Know that an unanswered prayer is an answer for you right here, right now.

God reveals his will to you day by day and moment by moment. Married people don’t know the long-term will of God for their lives any more than unmarried people. The reality is that my family could be taken away from me in an instant. No one is promised anything earthly for tomorrow. God promises us spiritual blessings but not physical or earthly ones.

Be careful with your expectations. You can create many hardships for yourself if you are very strong in your expectations. As an example, Matthew 20 has the story of the householder who promised his workers a penny for a day’s work. Later in the day, he hired other workers. In the evening, he was paying his workers, starting with the ones hired last, and gave them each a penny. Because of his generosity, the first workers expected more than he had promised them. Since they expected him to give them more than a penny, they murmured against him. Never have strong expectations for things that God hasn’t promised in the Bible, even if you feel like God has revealed it to you by his Spirit. It is far better to have a humble, open heart to God, family, and the brotherhood.

Fellowship

Fellowship with God’s people is another important step in the pathway to fulfillment. Don’t isolate yourself, but rather make yourself a part of God’s people.

“Then they that gladly received his word were baptized: and the same day there were added unto them about three thousand souls. 42 And they continued steadfastly in the apostles’ doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers” (Acts 2:41).

It can be easy to fall into the trap of feeling like you are different from everyone else and don’t fit in. Remember that everyone is unique, and together we make up the body of Christ. You are an important member and have gifts and abilities that are needed in your local fellowship. Spend time with people and find ways to be a blessing and help others.

Identity

Embrace your identity. You may wonder, who am I? Where do I fit in? This can be especially difficult if you have a strong desire to be married but are not. You might see others as becoming something that you desire to be but are not.

You might wonder, what is wrong with me that I am not married? This is wrong thinking. The reality is that there are many married people who are in a worse place than you. Be open when those around you have thoughts about changes you can and should make in your life, but don’t condemn yourself as not good enough and that others do not accept you. Ephesians chapter 1 says that you are chosen by God to be washed of your sins through the blood of Jesus and to be adopted as His child. You are accepted by God, and you are to be “to the praise of his glory!”

Purpose

The last step I am writing about is about purpose. What is one thing that you really enjoy doing that is a blessing to the church or Kingdom? God has a purpose for you to fulfill. You are a part of His kingdom that you can put time and energy into. God has called each one of us to be a servant, to follow in the footsteps of our Lord Jesus. It can be as simple as giving a glass of cold water in the name of Jesus. No task is too small or mundane to be a part of His kingdom. Be available. Have the heart of a servant. When you see a need, offer a helping hand or a listening ear.

“Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others. 5 Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus: 6 Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God: 7 But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men:” (Philippians 2:4)My wife and I recently celebrated our third anniversary. I was 38 and Jena 29 when we got married. This past spring we were blessed with a sweet little girl, Gianna. I wish I could say that we always lived out the things that I wrote in this article, but we are human and did come short at times. But we can both say from experience that the things I wrote are real and true. There is a pathway to joy and fulfillment as an unmarried person. Jena pursued midwifery and sacrificed a lot to serve mothers and babies. Always ready to drop whatever she was doing or jump out of bed in the middle of the night to go serve. I did a lot of Bible studies and also trips to the Middle East to study the Bible in a different measure. God has graciously given me the privilege to visit places where few people have been. I’ve been able to see where many of the people in the Bible lived and walked, including Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, David, and, best of all, Jesus. These people left behind a witness of faith and obedience. Let us follow them!

“Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us, 2 Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God. 3 For consider him that endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, lest ye be wearied and faint in your minds . . . (Hebrews 12:1-3).

“Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees; 13 And make straight paths for your feet, lest that which is lame be turned out of the way; but let it rather be healed. 14 Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord: 15 Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled . . . (Hebrews 12:12-15)

“Wherefore we receiving a kingdom which cannot be moved, let us have grace, whereby we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear” (Hebrews 12;28).

Kan jag ha ett uppfyllt hjärta om det finns en vision, ett hopp eller en dröm i mitt liv som ligger öde och ouppfylld? Måste jag gå genom livet och bära ett kors av smärta och ensamhet medan Gud besvarar mina vänners böner och ger dem önskningarna i deras hjärtan? Är det något fel på mig? Är min tro för svag? Har jag inte bett tillräckligt, överlämnat mig tillräckligt, varit lydig nog? Vad handlar livet om? Varför har jag inte frid och glädje? Har Gud en plan och ett syfte för mig?

”Du skall visa mig livets väg; i din närvaro är det fyllnad av glädje; vid din högra hand är det ljuvligheter för evigt” (Psaltaren 16:11).

”Och han skall vara som ett träd planterat vid vattenbäckar, som bär sin frukt i sin tid; lövet vissnar inte; och allt vad han gör skall lyckas” (Psaltaren 1:3).

Gud har en väg för var och en av oss som leder till ett uppfyllt hjärta. I Guds närvaro finns fullhet av glädje! Guds önskan är att ditt hjärta ska vara som ett träd vid flodstranden, fyllt av liv, hälsa, styrka och frukt. Han önskar att du ska uppleva nåd, glädje och frid i ditt dagliga liv. Gud vill fylla ditt hjärta med sina önskningar och syften. Han längtar efter att du söker hans vilja och plan. Om du vandrar på hans väg kommer du att fyllas med välsignelse och nåd. Detta betyder inte att varje begär du kan ha förverkligas (jag tror inte att det någonsin sker för någon i detta livet) utan snarare att ditt hjärta är fullt av Guds välsignelser. Ditt hjärta behöver inte kännas som en öken, Livets Vatten kan fylla det.

”Den som dricker av det vatten som jag skall ge honom skall aldrig mer törsta; utan det vatten jag skall ge honom skall bli i honom en källa med vatten som vältrar fram till evigt liv” (Johannes 4:14).

Var börjar uppfyllelse?

Uppfyllelse börjar i din relation med Gud. Känner du att Han är kall och fjärran, eller finner du glädje och frid i att be och vandra med honom? Vet du att dina synder är förlåtna och att du är accepterad som Hans barn? Lydar du Gud med ett villigt hjärta eller finns det områden i ditt liv där du motstår hans vilja som är uppenbarad i Bibeln? Att vandra i Guds kärlek och nåd är det viktigaste du kan göra i livet. Detta är det första steget på vägen till ett uppfyllt hjärta.

Om du kämpar i din relation med Gud och inte är säker på hans kärlek, förlåtelse och acceptans, här är några anvisningar från Bibeln för dig.

”Men den rättfärdighet som kommer av tron talar så här: Du skall inte säga i ditt hjärta: 'Vem skall stiga upp till himlen?' (det vill säga att föra ner Kristus från ovan); 7 eller: 'Vem skall stiga ner i avgrunden?' (det vill säga att föra upp Kristus från de döda). 8 Men vad säger den? Ordet är nära dig, i din mun och i ditt hjärta — det är tron som vi predikar. 9 Om du därför med din mun bekänner att Jesus är Herre och i ditt hjärta tror att Gud har uppväckt honom från de döda, skall du bli frälst. 10 Ty med hjärtat tror man till rättfärdighet, och med munnen bekänner man till frälsning” (Romarbrevet 10:6-10).

Du bör aldrig tänka att Kristus befinner sig på en otillgänglig plats och är otillgänglig för dig. Kristus görs känd för dig genom Bibeln, hans Helige Ande och genom hans skapelse. Otro, synd, olydnad och oförlåtelse mot andra kan hindra dig från att uppleva hans kärlek och nåd. Att öppna ditt hjärta för Honom i tro, tro i ditt hjärta och bekänna med din mun Herren Jesus, kommer att återställa din relation med Gud. Han kommer att tvätta bort din synd och ta emot dig som sitt barn. Kristus kom till denna jord för att försona oss med Gud. Han betalade priset för vår synd och skuld. Vi kan ta emot hans gåva av frälsning genom tro och omvändelse. Tro är helt enkelt att höra Guds Ord och ta emot det in i våra hjärtan.

När vi tar emot Guds Ord i våra hjärtan gör det oss kapabla att vara lydiga mot hans vilja. Vi väljer att tro allt som Gud har talat till oss i Bibeln. Vi släpper alla våra tvivel och omfamnar Hans Ord. Omvändelse är att vända sig bort från vår egen själviska vilja och våra syndiga vägar och välja att lyda Gud och hans Ord. I 1 Johannes 1:9 har Gud sagt att om vi bekänner våra synder skall Han förlåta oss. Tror du verkligen detta? Är det svårt för dig att acceptera att han kommer att förlåta dig? Det är omöjligt för Gud att ljuga, därför kan hans Ord och löften alltid litas på.

Praktiska sätt att vandra med Gud

”Det är alltså nu ingen fördömelse för dem som är i Kristus Jesus, som inte vandrar efter köttet utan efter Anden” (Romarbrevet 8:1).

Det finns andliga förutsättningar som behövs för att vandra med Gud. Om vi inte har ett rätt hjärta kommer dessa praktiska saker inte egentligen hjälpa oss att vandra med Gud. Det blir bara en tom aktivitet utan verklig mening och liten nytta.

Med våra hjärtan fulla av tro och kärlek behöver vi tro allt i Bibeln. Vi måste tro all dess historia, allt den säger om mannen Jesus, alla profetior och all den vägledning Gud ger oss i Ordet.

Vi behöver också ett överlämnat hjärta och välja att följa och lyda Gud i allt. Det finns inget område där vi väljer att försumma eller trotsa. Vi måste ha bekänt våra synder och vara födda på nytt genom Guds Ande.

Be. För dig själv, Guds rike, din familj, församlingen, grannar, änkor och änklingar, föräldralösa, missionärer, regeringar och sjuka. Be för dem som mist sina kära, hungriga människor, människor i fängelse och människor som behöver frälsning. Be att Gud skickar arbetare ut i vingården.

Studera Ordet. Memorera det och läs det för andra. Diskutera det.

Sjung lovsånger till Gud! Gud har varit så barmhärtig mot dig. Gläd dig i din frälsning!

”Och att hedningarna må prisa Gud för hans barmhärtighet; såsom det är skrivet: 'Därför vill jag tacka dig bland hedningarna och sjunga ditt namn.' 10 Och åter säger han: 'Gäd er, ni hedningar, med hans folk.' 11 Och åter: 'Pris Herren, alla hedningar, och lova honom, alla folk' ” (Romarbrevet 15:9).

Inre tillfredsställelse

Ett annat stort steg på vägen till ett uppfyllt hjärta är inre tillfredsställelse. Du kan aldrig vara uppfylld om du inte är tillfreds i vetskapen om att du är i Guds vilja.

”Er samtal skall vara utan girighet; varliga nöjda med det ni har; ty han har sagt: Jag skall aldrig lämna dig eller överge dig. 6 Så att vi frimodigt kan säga: Herren är min hjälpare, jag skall inte frukta; vad kan en människa göra mot mig?” (Hebreerbrevet 13:5).

Vad är girighet? Min definition av girighet är att ha en stark önskan efter något som ligger utanför Guds vilja för mig just nu. Vanligtvis driver girighet dig att bryta mot skriften och Guds vilja för att försöka skaffa det du begär. Till exempel, om du är girig efter pengar kommer du att tendera att göra oetiska saker eller försumma att följa Bibelns riktning i din strävan efter pengar. Du kan fuska, stjäla, lura, ta överpriser eller bli en arbetsnarkoman och försaka Gud, familjen, församlingen eller de behövande.

Gud har gett oss begär, och det är en god sak att förfölja dem om vårt hjärta är överlämnat, söker Guds vilja och förföljer den enligt den vägledning som ges i Bibeln. Sträva efter att gå framåt, men tvinga aldrig din egen vilja. Var öppen för de människor som Gud har satt i ditt liv för vägledning.

Du kanske är i den åldern när dina vänner gifter sig. Du önskar också gifta dig, men alla dörrar slår igen i ditt ansikte. Det verkar som om Gud uppenbarar sin vilja för andra men inte för dig. Vet att en obesvarad bön är ett svar för dig här och nu.

Gud uppenbarar sin vilja för dig dag för dag och stund för stund. Gifta människor känner inte Guds långsiktiga vilja för deras liv mer än ogifta människor gör. Verkligheten är att min familj kan tas ifrån mig på ett ögonblick. Ingen är lovad något jordiskt för morgondagen. Gud lovar oss andliga välsignelser men inte fysiska eller jordiska sådana.

Var försiktig med dina förväntningar. Du kan skapa många svårigheter för dig själv om du har mycket starka förväntningar. Som exempel finns berättelsen i Matteus 20 om husbonden som lovade sina arbetare en denar för en dags arbete. Senare på dagen anställde han andra arbetare. På kvällen betalade han sina arbetare, med att börja med dem som anställdes sist, och gav dem var sin denar. På grund av hans frikostighet förväntade sig de första arbetarna mer än vad han lovat dem. Eftersom de väntat sig att han skulle ge dem mer än en denar, klagade de på honom. Ha aldrig starka förväntningar på saker som Gud inte har lovat i Bibeln, även om du känner att Gud har uppenbarat det för dig genom sin Ande. Det är mycket bättre att ha ett ödmjukt, öppet hjärta inför Gud, familjen och brödraskapet.

Gemenskap

Gemenskap med Guds folk är ett annat viktigt steg på vägen mot uppfyllelse. Isolera dig inte, utan gör dig i stället till en del av Guds folk.

”Och de som tog emot hans ord med glädje blev döpta, och samma dag tillfogades dem ungefär tre tusen själar. 42 Och de höll sig troget vid apostlarnas undervisning och gemenskapen, vid brödbrytelsen och vid bönerna” (Apostlagärningarna 2:41).

Det kan vara lätt att falla i fällan att känna att du är annorlunda än alla andra och inte passar in. Kom ihåg att alla är unika, och tillsammans utgör vi Kristi kropp. Du är en viktig medlem och har gåvor och förmågor som behövs i din lokala gemenskap. Tillbringa tid med människor och hitta sätt att vara en välsignelse och hjälpa andra.

Identitet

Anamma din identitet. Du undrar kanske, vem är jag? Var passar jag in? Detta kan vara särskilt svårt om du har en stark önskan att bli gift men inte är det. Du kanske ser andra bli något som du önskar vara men inte är.

Du kanske undrar, vad är fel på mig som inte är gift? Detta är felaktigt tänkande. Verkligheten är att det finns många gifta människor som har det sämre än du. Var öppen när de omkring dig har tankar om förändringar du kan och bör göra i ditt liv, men döm dig inte själv som otillräcklig och tro att andra inte accepterar dig. Efesierbrevet kapitel 1 säger att du är utvald av Gud för att bli renad från dina synder genom Jesu blod och bli adopterad som Hans barn. Du är accepterad av Gud, och du är till ”hans lof”!

Syfte

Det sista steget jag skriver om handlar om syfte. Vad är en sak som du verkligen tycker om att göra som är en välsignelse för församlingen eller Guds rike? Gud har ett syfte för dig att uppfylla. Du är en del av Hans rike som du kan lägga tid och energi på. Gud har kallat var och en av oss att vara en tjänare, att följa i vår Herre Jesu fotspår. Det kan vara så enkelt som att ge ett glas kallt vatten i Jesu namn. Ingen uppgift är för liten eller vardaglig för att vara en del av Hans rike. Var tillgänglig. Ha ett tjänande hjärta. När du ser ett behov, erbjud en hjälpande hand eller ett lyssnande öra.

”Se inte var och en på det som tillhör honom själv, utan var och en också på det som tillhör andra. 5 Låt detta sinne vara i er som också var i Kristus Jesus: 6 han, som i Guds gestalt var, ansåg det icke såsom rov att vara Gud lik; 7 utan gav avkall på sig själv och tog till sig tjänarens gestalt och blev människolik” (Filipperbrevet 2:4). Min fru och jag firade nyligen vårt tredje år tillsammans. Jag var 38 och Jena 29 när vi gifte oss. I våras blev vi välsignade med en liten söt flicka, Gianna. Jag önskar att jag kunde säga att vi alltid levde ut det jag skrev i denna artikel, men vi är människor och har ibland fallit kort. Men vi kan båda säga av erfarenhet att det jag skrev är verkligt och sant. Det finns en väg till glädje och uppfyllelse som ogift person. Jena utbildade sig till barnmorska och offrade mycket för att tjäna mödrar och barn. Alltid redo att släppa vad hon gjorde eller hoppa upp ur sängen mitt i natten för att gå och tjäna. Jag gjorde många bibelstudier och också resor till Mellanöstern för att studera Bibeln i en annan måttstock. Gud har nådigt gett mig förmånen att besöka platser där få människor varit. Jag har kunnat se var många av människorna i Bibeln levde och vandrade, inklusive Noa, Abraham, Isak, Jakob, Mose, David och, bäst av allt, Jesus. Dessa människor lämnade ett vittnesbörd om tro och lydnad. Låt oss följa dem!

”Därför, eftersom vi är omgivna av ett så stort vittnesskare, låt oss kasta av oss allt som tynger och synden som så lätt fångar oss, och låt oss löpa uthålligt i det lopp som ligger framför oss, 2 med blicken fäst vid Jesus, tronfullhetens upphovsman och fullkomnare, som för den glädje som låg framför honom utstod korset och föraktade skämslen och satt sig ner vid Guds trons högra sida. 3 Betrakta honom som uthärdade sådant motstånd från syndare emot sig, för att ni inte skall bli mattade och tappa modet i era tankar . . . ” (Hebreerbrevet 12:1-3).

”Därför lyft upp de hängande händerna och de svaga knäna, 13 och gör raka steg för era fötter, så att den haltande inte vänds utanför utan hellre blir botad. 14 Sträva efter frid med alla och efter helgelse, utan vilken ingen skall se Herren. 15 Se noga till att ingen uteblir från Guds nåd, att ingen bitterrots rot skjuter upp och därigenom många blir smittade . . . ” (Hebreerbrevet 12:12-15)

”Därför, eftersom vi får ett oflyttbart rike, låt oss vara tacksamma och därigenom tjäna Gud på ett behagligt sätt med vördnad och gudsfruktan” (Hebreerbrevet 12;28).

When I was converted, I had never heard the term Anabaptist. I had never heard much about witnessing to others. I remember thinking about all my friends who didn’t know anything about what had just happened to me. My girlfriend of seven years didn’t understand. One thing kept going through my mind: “I need to tell them!” Something good had happened to me, and everyone needed to know that the same could happen to them! I remember a time when my brother and I were thinking of a place where we could tell many people about Jesus. We decided to go to a major league baseball game. I was nervous, I was scared, and I will never forget what happened. I had never spoken in front of a large crowd before, but when I opened my mouth, God filled it.

I did not only go and talk to people I did not know. When I saw an old friend, I would tell them what happened to me. They would usually say they had heard it before and try to convince me to settle down and relax. I will be the first to admit that I made some mistakes in those first few years. I noticed, to my astonishment, that while many people didn’t like me, it was the people who said they were Christians who appeared to dislike me the most. One day I was visiting with an older man who said he had been a Christian most of his life. During the discussion, he pointed up to a lightbulb and said, “‘Do you see that lightbulb? It’s not speaking.” I was shocked. He was telling me that, yes, while Jesus says we are the light of the world, lights are supposed to shine quietly. They don’t speak.

I was astonished. Was this true? I went home to do a Bible study. It wasn’t long before I found verses like Matthew 4:23, “And Jesus went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the people.” Then in Matthew 9, when Jesus “saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd. Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few; Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest” (Matthew 9:36-38).

It seems to me that wherever Jesus went, He was talking to people about the kingdom. I have seen people witnessing about God, but sometimes in an offensive way. But does that mean we shouldn’t witness? If you read the book of Acts, that’s nearly all you see—the Gospel going out! In one account the authorities captured the disciples and said they could go free if they would only be quiet. However, the disciples said they could not. “For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard” (Acts 4:20). Later they were silenced—by death.

Sometime later I heard about these people called Anabaptists. As I studied them, I began to see how they too, would not be silent. I ordered a copy of The Martyr’s Mirror and was astounded when I read about these people who lived like the disciples. They fulfilled the things Jesus said, “And ye shall be hated of all men for my name's sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved” (Matt. 10:22). And in Romans 8:36, “As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter.”

Dear brothers and sisters, I believe the fire is going out. I hear many of our Anabaptist people talking about living a quiet and peaceable life. Jesus tells us in the parable of the sower, “He also that received seed among the thorns is he that heareth the word; and the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, and he becometh unfruitful” (Matt. 13:22). Could that be where many of us are at? We live in the free land of America where money seems easy to obtain. Is it possible we have become deceived by our own wealth and the cares of this world? Have we become like the world to avoid being persecuted by it?

Many years ago, a group of Anabaptists fled persecution and moved to a country where there was less oppression. They opened a furniture shop to support themselves, but they couldn’t sell any furniture because they were the dreaded Anabaptists. Soon, the situation became desperate because they didn’t have money to buy food. One day a wealthy man walked into the shop. All the workers stopped what they were doing. They thought to themselves, “Maybe this man will buy something, and we can eat!” An old brother approached the possible client and asked him if he knew Jesus. After a short chat, the man stormed out of the store in a fit of anger. The hungry workers asked the old man why he had scared away their only chance at a sale. He explained that for this man to know Jesus was far more important than for them to earn some money.

In the mindset of the early Anabaptists, the Gospel of Jesus was number one. As in Acts, they could not but speak of the things they had seen and heard. And they, too, were “killed all the day long”.

So, what do we do with the verse about a quiet and peaceable life? The verse is found in 1 Timothy 2:1-2: “I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty.” What did the apostle Paul mean when he wrote this? Did he mean that we should be quiet about the gospel and never challenge a sinner? It is hard to believe that Paul is telling us to do something he never did, something that Christ Himself never did. In fact, no one in the scriptures who followed God was quiet about their faith. In numerous accounts of early Christians who had been arrested for their faith, the authorities would plead with them to just be quiet! But they refused, just as the disciples did. They also chose death, rather than a quiet and peaceable life.

One young Anabaptist who was arrested left behind his dear wife expecting their first child. The authorities waited for the child to be born then brought the infant to the new father in prison. They told him he was now a father and could go home and be with his wife and son. He could even continue to believe the same way, but he had to keep quiet and not speak out against sin in the state church. The young father refused. For him, being quiet was not an option. They burned him at the stake.

So, what does 1 Timothy 2:1-2 mean? It seems that the Christians in the Bible and early church were all about spreading the gospel, all about the church of Christ. They went about preaching the gospel, holding meetings in the mountains, woods, or anywhere people would come. That was their life. In the verse in 1 Timothy 2, Paul is saying we should pray that the authorities will let us live in peace so we can spread the gospel. Christians should be out spreading the word and pressing into the kingdom. Our prayer is that the authorities will let us live in peace, while we serve the Prince of peace.

Today it’s easy to be a Christian when you settle down and live a quiet and peaceable life, never challenging a sinner or correcting a brother. But who said it would be easy?

When we were living in Haiti, we taught our church about the cost of following Jesus. It was amazing to hear the Haitians’ testimonies of applying Jesus’ teaching to their lives. One time, two members told us they were about to lose their jobs because of following the gospel. To hear them make a stand for following truth made me happy. Another sister in the church told me that the school her children attended wore uniforms and the girls were required to wear pants. When she sent her daughter to school in a modest dress, she came home with a note from the principal saying she was not to return to school wearing that thing.

1 Peter 4:14 says, “If ye be reproached for the name of Christ, happy are ye; for the spirit of glory and of God resteth upon you: on their part he is evil spoken of, but on your part he is glorified.”

True joy comes from suffering. Suffering comes from obeying Jesus. Are we too busy with trivial matters while the world goes to hell? Let us follow Jesus like the early Christians, where men could not deny that the power of God was working in them. We have something everyone needs. What are we waiting for? Let’s reunite, gather back together, deny ourselves, take up the cross, and follow Him!

Όταν μεταστράφηκα, δεν είχα ποτέ ακούσει τον όρο Αναβαπτιστής. Δεν είχα ακούσει πολλά για το κήρυγμα σε άλλους. Θυμάμαι που σκεφτόμουν όλους τους φίλους μου που δεν ήξεραν τίποτα για ό,τι μου είχε μόλις συμβεί. Η κοπέλα μου των επτά χρόνων δεν καταλάβαινε. Ένα πράγμα επαναλαμβανόταν στο μυαλό μου: «Πρέπει να τους το πω!» Κάτι καλό μου είχε συμβεί και όλοι έπρεπε να ξέρουν ότι το ίδιο μπορούσε να τους συμβεί και αυτούς! Θυμάμαι μια φορά που εγώ και ο αδελφός μου ήμασταν σκεφτόμενοι ένα μέρος όπου θα μπορούσαμε να πούμε σε πολλούς ανθρώπους για τον Ιησού. Αποφασίσαμε να πάμε σε έναν αγώνα του μεγάλου πρωταθλήματος μπέιζμπολ. Ήμουν νευρικός, φοβισμένος, και δεν θα ξεχάσω ποτέ τι συνέβη. Δεν είχα μιλήσει ποτέ μπροστά σε μεγάλο πλήθος πριν, αλλά όταν άνοιξα το στόμα μου, ο Θεός το γέμισε.

Δεν πήγαινα μόνο και μιλούσα σε άγνωστους ανθρώπους. Όταν έβλεπα έναν παλιό φίλο, του έλεγα τι μου είχε συμβεί. Συνήθως έλεγαν ότι το είχαν ακούσει ξανά και προσπαθούσαν να με πείσουν να ησυχάσω και να χαλαρώσω. Θα είμαι ο πρώτος που θα παραδεχτώ ότι έκανα μερικά λάθη εκείνα τα πρώτα χρόνια. Παρατήρησα, προς έκπληξή μου, ότι ενώ πολλοί άνθρωποι δεν με συμπαθούσαν, ήταν οι άνθρωποι που έλεγαν ότι ήταν χριστιανοί που φαινόντουσαν να με αντιπαθούν περισσότερο. Μια μέρα επισκεπτόμουν έναν μεγαλύτερο άντρα που έλεγε ότι είχε υπάρξει χριστιανός το μεγαλύτερο μέρος της ζωής του. Κατά τη διάρκεια της συζήτησης, έδειξε με το δάχτυλο μία λάμπα και είπε, «Βλέπεις εκείνη τη λάμπα; Δεν μιλάει.» Έμεινα άναυδος. Μου έλεγε ότι, ναι, ενώ ο Ιησούς λέει ότι είμαστε το φως του κόσμου, τα φώτα προορίζονται να λάμπουν ήσυχα. Δεν μιλούν.

Έμεινα κατάπληκτος. Ήταν αυτό αλήθεια; Πήγα στο σπίτι για να κάνω μια μελέτη στη Βίβλο. Δεν πέρασε πολύς καιρός πριν βρήκα εδάφια όπως το Ματθαίος 4:23, «Και περιήρχετο ο Ἰησοῦς εις όλην την Γαλιλαίαν, διδάσκων εν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αυτών, κηρύσσων το ευαγγέλιον της βασιλείας, και θεραπεύων πάσαν νόσον και πάσαν νόσον εν τω λαώ.» Τότε στο Ματθαίος 9, όταν ο Ιησούς «είδε τα πλήθη, εσπλαγχνίσθη επ’ αυτών, επειδή εκλυόμενοι και εδιασκορπίζοντο ήσαν ως πρόβατα μη έχοντα ποιμένα. Τότε λέγει προς τους μαθητάς αυτού· Η θερισμός ωστόσο πολύς, οι δε εργαζόμενοι ολίγοι· δεήθητε ουν προς τον κύριον του θερισμού, ίνα εκβάλῃ εργαζομένους εις τον θερισμόν αυτού» (Ματθ. 9:36-38).

Μου φαίνεται ότι όπου κι αν πήγαινε ο Ιησούς, μιλούσε στους ανθρώπους για τη βασιλεία. Έχω δει ανθρώπους να μαρτυρούν για τον Θεό, αλλά μερικές φορές με προσβλητικό τρόπο. Αλλά σημαίνει αυτό ότι δεν πρέπει να μαρτυρούμε; Αν διαβάσεις το βιβλίο των Πράξεων, αυτό σχεδόν όλα όσα βλέπεις—το Ευαγγέλιο που διαδίδεται! Σε ένα επεισόδιο οι αρχές συνέλεξαν τους μαθητές και είπαν ότι μπορούσαν να αφεθούν ελεύθεροι αν απλά κρατούσαν το στόμα τους κλειστό. Ωστόσο, οι μαθητές είπαν ότι δεν μπορούσαν. «Ου δύναται δε ημείς μη λαλήσαι τα όσα εωράκαμεν και ηκούσαμεν» (Πράξεις 4:20). Αργότερα σιώπησαν—με το θάνατο.

Κάποια στιγμή αργότερα άκουσα για αυτούς τους ανθρώπους που ονομάζονταν Αναβαπτιστές. Καθώς τους μελετούσα, άρχισα να βλέπω πώς κι αυτοί δεν ήθελαν να σωπάσουν. Παρήγγειλα ένα αντίτυπο του The Martyr’s Mirror και έμεινα κατάπληκτος όταν διάβαζα για αυτούς τους ανθρώπους που ζούσαν όπως οι μαθητές. Εκπλήρωναν όσα είπε ο Ιησούς, «και μισηθήσεσθε υπό πάντων δι’ το όνομα μου· όστις δ’ αν αντήξει έως τέλους, ούτος σωθήσεται» (Ματθ. 10:22). Και στη Ρωμαίους 8:36, «καθώς γέγραπται· Δι’ εσέ κατακτείνεσμέν τε καθ’ ημέραν· ελογίσθημεν ως πρόβατα σφαγιας.»

Αγαπητοί αδελφοί και αδελφές, πιστεύω ότι η φωτιά σβήνει. Ακούω πολλούς από τον αναβαπτιστικό μας λαό να μιλούν για το να ζουν μια ήσυχη και ειρηνική ζωή. Ο Ιησούς μας λέει στη παραβολή του σπορέα, «Ο δε ελθόν εις τας ακανθάς, εκείνος εστίν ο τω λόγω ακουών· και η μέριμνα του αιώνος τούτου και η απατηλότης των πλουσίων πνίγουσι τον λόγον, και άκαρπος γίγνεται» (Ματθ. 13:22). Μήπως αυτό είναι το σημείο όπου πολλοί από εμάς βρισκόμαστε; Ζούμε στη ελεύθερη χώρα της Αμερικής όπου τα χρήματα φαίνεται εύκολα να αποκτώνται. Είναι πιθανό να έχουμε εξαπατηθεί από τον δικό μας πλούτο και τις μέριμνες αυτού του κόσμου; Έχουμε γίνει σαν τον κόσμο για να αποφύγουμε να διωχθούμε απ’ αυτόν;

Πολλά χρόνια πριν, μια ομάδα Αναβαπτιστών διέφυγε από διωγμό και μετακόμισε σε μια χώρα όπου υπήρχε λιγότερη καταπίεση. Άνοιξαν ένα κατάστημα επίπλων για να συντηρηθούν, αλλά δεν μπορούσαν να πουλήσουν κανένα έπιπλο επειδή ήταν οι μισητοί Αναβαπτιστές. Σύντομα η κατάσταση έγινε απελπιστική γιατί δεν είχαν χρήματα να αγοράσουν τρόφιμα. Μια μέρα ένας πλούσιος άντρας μπήκε στο κατάστημα. Όλοι οι εργάτες σταμάτησαν ό,τι έκαναν. Σκέφτηκαν μέσα τους, «Ίσως αυτός ο άντρας θα αγοράσει κάτι και θα φάμε!» Ένας γέροντας αδελφός πλησίασε τον πιθανό πελάτη και τον ρώτησε αν γνώριζε τον Ιησού. Μετά από μια σύντομη συζήτηση, ο άντρας εξαγριώθηκε και έφυγε τρέχοντας από το μαγαζί. Οι πεινασμένοι εργάτες ρώτησαν τον γέροντα γιατί είχε διώξει την μόνη τους ευκαιρία για πώληση. Εκείνος εξήγησε ότι για αυτόν ήταν πολύ πιο σημαντικό να γνωρίσει ο άντρας τον Ιησού παρά να κερδίσουν κάποιο χρήμα.

Στην νοοτροπία των πρώτων Αναβαπτιστών, το Ευαγγέλιο του Ιησού ήταν το πρώτο. Όπως στις Πράξεις, δεν μπορούσαν παρά να μιλήσουν για τα όσα είχαν δει και ακούσει. Και αυτοί, επίσης, «κατακτέννυνται καθ’ ημέραν».

Λοιπόν, τι κάνουμε με το εδάφιο για μια ήσυχη και ειρηνική ζωή; Το εδάφιο βρίσκεται στην 1 Τιμόθεο 2:1-2: «Παρακαλώ ουν πρώτον απαραιτήτως, ποιούντων ικεσίας, προσευχάς, αιτήσεις, ευχαριστίας υπέρ πάντων ανθρώπων· υπέρ των βασιλέων και πάντων των εν υψηλοίς, ίνα αγάθως ησυχάσωμεν και ευσχημονώμεν εν πάση ευσεβείαι και σεμνότητι.» Τι ήθελε να πει ο απόστολος Παύλος όταν έγραψε αυτό; Εννοούσε μήπως ότι πρέπει να είμαστε σιωπηλοί για το ευαγγέλιο και να μην αμφισβητούμε ποτέ έναν αμαρτωλό; Είναι δύσκολο να πιστέψει κανείς ότι ο Παύλος μας λέει να κάνουμε κάτι που δεν έκανε ποτέ ο ίδιος, κάτι που ο Χριστός ο Ίδιος δεν έκανε ποτέ. Στην πραγματικότητα, κανένας στις Γραφές που ακολούθησε τον Θεό δεν ήταν σιωπηλός για την πίστη του. Σε πολυάριθμες αφηγήσεις πρώιμων χριστιανών που είχαν συλληφθεί για την πίστη τους, οι αρχές τους παρακαλούσαν να σωπάσουν! Αλλά αυτοί αρνούνταν, όπως έκαναν και οι μαθητές. Επίλεξαν επίσης το θάνατο, παρά μια ήσυχη και ειρηνική ζωή.

Ένας νεαρός Αναβαπτιστής που συνελήφθη άφησε πίσω του την αγαπημένη του γυναίκα που περίμενε το πρώτο τους παιδί. Οι αρχές περίμεναν να γεννηθεί το παιδί και τότε έφεραν το βρέφος στον νέο πατέρα στη φυλακή. Του είπαν ότι τώρα ήταν πατέρας και μπορούσε να επιστρέψει στο σπίτι και να είναι με τη γυναίκα και τον γιο του. Μπορούσε ακόμη και να συνεχίσει να πιστεύει με τον ίδιο τρόπο, αλλά έπρεπε να σιωπήσει και να μην μιλάει κατά της αμαρτίας στην κρατική εκκλησία. Ο νέος πατέρας αρνήθηκε. Για εκείνον, η σιωπή δεν ήταν επιλογή. Τον έκαψαν στην πυρά.

Λοιπόν, τι σημαίνουν οι 1 Τιμόθεο 2:1-2; Φαίνεται ότι οι χριστιανοί στην Αγία Γραφή και στην πρώιμη εκκλησία είχαν ως σκοπό τη διάδοση του ευαγγελίου, την οικοδόμηση της εκκλησίας του Χριστού. Περιφέρονταν κηρύσσοντας το ευαγγέλιο, διοργανώνοντας συναντήσεις στα βουνά, στα δάση ή οπουδήποτε θα πήγαιναν άνθρωποι. Αυτή ήταν η ζωή τους. Στο εδάφιο της 1 Τιμόθεου 2, ο Παύλος λέει ότι πρέπει να προσευχόμαστε ώστε οι αρχές να μας αφήσουν να ζήσουμε ειρηνικά, ώστε να μπορούμε να διαδίδουμε το ευαγγέλιο. Οι χριστιανοί θα πρέπει να βγαίνουν έξω διαδίδοντας τον λόγο και διεισδύοντας στη βασιλεία. Η προσευχή μας είναι οι αρχές να μας αφήσουν να ζήσουμε ειρηνικά, ενώ υπηρετούμε τον Πρίγκιπα της ειρήνης.

Σήμερα είναι εύκολο να είσαι χριστιανός όταν εγκατασταθείς και ζεις μια ήσυχη και ειρηνική ζωή, ποτέ μην αμφισβητώντας έναν αμαρτωλό ή διορθώνοντας έναν αδελφό. Αλλά ποιος είπε ότι θα είναι εύκολο;

Όταν ζούσαμε στην Αϊτή, διδάξαμε την εκκλησία μας για το κόστος του να ακολουθείς τον Ιησού. Ήταν εκπληκτικό να ακούει κανείς τις μαρτυρίες των Αϊτινών για το πώς εφάρμοζαν τη διδασκαλία του Ιησού στη ζωή τους. Μια φορά, δύο μέλη μας είπαν ότι κινδύνευαν να χάσουν τις δουλειές τους εξαιτίας του ότι ακολουθούσαν το ευαγγέλιο. Το να τους ακούς να πάρουν θέση για την αλήθεια με έκανε χαρούμενο. Μια άλλη αδελφή στην εκκλησία μου είπε ότι το σχολείο που παρακολουθούσαν τα παιδιά της είχε στολή και τα κορίτσια ήταν υποχρεωμένα να φορούν παντελόνια. Όταν έστειλε την κόρη της στο σχολείο με ένα σεμνό φόρεμα, η κόρη επέστρεψε με σημείωμα από τη διευθύντρια που έλεγε να μην επιστρέψει στο σχολείο φορώντας εκείνο το πράγμα.

1 Πέτρου 4:14 λέει, «Εάν δε υμείς καυχώσθαι επί το όνομα του Χριστού, μακάριοι είστε· δι’ ου γαρ η δόξα και το πνεύμα του Θεού αναπαύεται επ’ υμίν· επί δε τους λοιπούς αυτό κακόν ρημάζεται, επί δε υμάς δοξάζεται.»

Η αληθινή χαρά προέρχεται από τον πόνο. Ο πόνος προέρχεται από την υπακοή στον Ιησού. Είμαστε πολύ απασχολημένοι με ασήμαντα ζητήματα ενώ ο κόσμος πηγαίνει στην κόλαση; Ας ακολουθήσουμε τον Ιησού όπως οι πρώτοι χριστιανοί, όπου οι άνθρωποι δεν μπορούσαν να αρνηθούν ότι η δύναμη του Θεού εργαζόταν μέσα τους. Έχουμε κάτι που χρειάζεται ο καθένας. Τι περιμένουμε; Ας ξαναενωθούμε, ας μαζευτούμε μαζί, ας αρνηθούμε τον εαυτό μας, ας σηκώσουμε τον σταυρό και ας Τον ακολουθήσουμε!

When I was converted, I had never heard the term Anabaptist. I had never heard much about witnessing to others. I remember thinking about all my friends who didn’t know anything about what had just happened to me. My girlfriend of seven years didn’t understand. One thing kept going through my mind: “I need to tell them!” Something good had happened to me, and everyone needed to know that the same could happen to them! I remember a time when my brother and I were thinking of a place where we could tell many people about Jesus. We decided to go to a major league baseball game. I was nervous, I was scared, and I will never forget what happened. I had never spoken in front of a large crowd before, but when I opened my mouth, God filled it.

I did not only go and talk to people I did not know. When I saw an old friend, I would tell them what happened to me. They would usually say they had heard it before and try to convince me to settle down and relax. I will be the first to admit that I made some mistakes in those first few years. I noticed, to my astonishment, that while many people didn’t like me, it was the people who said they were Christians who appeared to dislike me the most. One day I was visiting with an older man who said he had been a Christian most of his life. During the discussion, he pointed up to a lightbulb and said, “‘Do you see that lightbulb? It’s not speaking.” I was shocked. He was telling me that, yes, while Jesus says we are the light of the world, lights are supposed to shine quietly. They don’t speak.

I was astonished. Was this true? I went home to do a Bible study. It wasn’t long before I found verses like Matthew 4:23, “And Jesus went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the people.” Then in Matthew 9, when Jesus “saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd. Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few; Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest” (Matthew 9:36-38).

It seems to me that wherever Jesus went, He was talking to people about the kingdom. I have seen people witnessing about God, but sometimes in an offensive way. But does that mean we shouldn’t witness? If you read the book of Acts, that’s nearly all you see—the Gospel going out! In one account the authorities captured the disciples and said they could go free if they would only be quiet. However, the disciples said they could not. “For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard” (Acts 4:20). Later they were silenced—by death.

Sometime later I heard about these people called Anabaptists. As I studied them, I began to see how they too, would not be silent. I ordered a copy of The Martyr’s Mirror and was astounded when I read about these people who lived like the disciples. They fulfilled the things Jesus said, “And ye shall be hated of all men for my name's sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved” (Matt. 10:22). And in Romans 8:36, “As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter.”

Dear brothers and sisters, I believe the fire is going out. I hear many of our Anabaptist people talking about living a quiet and peaceable life. Jesus tells us in the parable of the sower, “He also that received seed among the thorns is he that heareth the word; and the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, and he becometh unfruitful” (Matt. 13:22). Could that be where many of us are at? We live in the free land of America where money seems easy to obtain. Is it possible we have become deceived by our own wealth and the cares of this world? Have we become like the world to avoid being persecuted by it?

Many years ago, a group of Anabaptists fled persecution and moved to a country where there was less oppression. They opened a furniture shop to support themselves, but they couldn’t sell any furniture because they were the dreaded Anabaptists. Soon, the situation became desperate because they didn’t have money to buy food. One day a wealthy man walked into the shop. All the workers stopped what they were doing. They thought to themselves, “Maybe this man will buy something, and we can eat!” An old brother approached the possible client and asked him if he knew Jesus. After a short chat, the man stormed out of the store in a fit of anger. The hungry workers asked the old man why he had scared away their only chance at a sale. He explained that for this man to know Jesus was far more important than for them to earn some money.

In the mindset of the early Anabaptists, the Gospel of Jesus was number one. As in Acts, they could not but speak of the things they had seen and heard. And they, too, were “killed all the day long”.

So, what do we do with the verse about a quiet and peaceable life? The verse is found in 1 Timothy 2:1-2: “I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty.” What did the apostle Paul mean when he wrote this? Did he mean that we should be quiet about the gospel and never challenge a sinner? It is hard to believe that Paul is telling us to do something he never did, something that Christ Himself never did. In fact, no one in the scriptures who followed God was quiet about their faith. In numerous accounts of early Christians who had been arrested for their faith, the authorities would plead with them to just be quiet! But they refused, just as the disciples did. They also chose death, rather than a quiet and peaceable life.

One young Anabaptist who was arrested left behind his dear wife expecting their first child. The authorities waited for the child to be born then brought the infant to the new father in prison. They told him he was now a father and could go home and be with his wife and son. He could even continue to believe the same way, but he had to keep quiet and not speak out against sin in the state church. The young father refused. For him, being quiet was not an option. They burned him at the stake.

So, what does 1 Timothy 2:1-2 mean? It seems that the Christians in the Bible and early church were all about spreading the gospel, all about the church of Christ. They went about preaching the gospel, holding meetings in the mountains, woods, or anywhere people would come. That was their life. In the verse in 1 Timothy 2, Paul is saying we should pray that the authorities will let us live in peace so we can spread the gospel. Christians should be out spreading the word and pressing into the kingdom. Our prayer is that the authorities will let us live in peace, while we serve the Prince of peace.

Today it’s easy to be a Christian when you settle down and live a quiet and peaceable life, never challenging a sinner or correcting a brother. But who said it would be easy?

When we were living in Haiti, we taught our church about the cost of following Jesus. It was amazing to hear the Haitians’ testimonies of applying Jesus’ teaching to their lives. One time, two members told us they were about to lose their jobs because of following the gospel. To hear them make a stand for following truth made me happy. Another sister in the church told me that the school her children attended wore uniforms and the girls were required to wear pants. When she sent her daughter to school in a modest dress, she came home with a note from the principal saying she was not to return to school wearing that thing.

1 Peter 4:14 says, “If ye be reproached for the name of Christ, happy are ye; for the spirit of glory and of God resteth upon you: on their part he is evil spoken of, but on your part he is glorified.”

True joy comes from suffering. Suffering comes from obeying Jesus. Are we too busy with trivial matters while the world goes to hell? Let us follow Jesus like the early Christians, where men could not deny that the power of God was working in them. We have something everyone needs. What are we waiting for? Let’s reunite, gather back together, deny ourselves, take up the cross, and follow Him!

عندما تحولت، لم أكن قد سمعت من قبل مصطلح أنابابتيست. لم أكن قد سمعت كثيرًا عن الشهادة للآخرين. أذكر أنني فكرت في كل أصدقائي الذين لم يعرفوا شيئًا عما حدث لي للتو. لم تفهم صديقتي التي امتدت علاقتي معها سبع سنوات. كان شيء واحد يرد في ذهني باستمرار: «يجب أن أخبرهم!» حدث شيء جيد لي، وكان على الجميع أن يعرف أن الشيء نفسه قد يحدث لهم! أذكر مرة حين فكرت أنا وأخي في مكان حيث يمكننا أن نخبر الكثير من الناس عن يسوع. قررنا الذهاب إلى مباراة دوري كُبرى في كرة القاعدة. كنت متوترًا، خائفًا، ولن أنسى ما حدث أبدًا. لم أكن قد تكلمت أمام جمهور كبير من قبل، ولكن عندما فتحت فمي، ملأه الله.

لم أكتفِ بالحديث إلى أشخاص لا أعرفهم فحسب. عندما رأيت صديقًا قديمًا، كنت أخبره بما حدث لي. كانوا عادة يقولون إنهم سمعوا ذلك من قبل ويحاولون إقناعي بالاستقرار والهدوء. سأكون أول من يعترف بأنني ارتكبت بعض الأخطاء في تلك السنوات القليلة الأولى. لاحظت، لدهشتي، أنه بينما لم يكن الكثير من الناس يحبونني، بدا أن أكثر من يكرهونني هم من يزعمون أنهم مسيحيون. في يومٍ ما كنت أزور رجلاً مسنًا قال إنه كان مسيحيًا معظم حياته. أثناء النقاش، أشار إلى لمبة وقال: «أترى تلك اللمبة؟ إنها لا تتكلم.» صُدمت. كان يخبرني أنه، نعم، بينما يقول يسوع إننا نور العالم، فالمصابيح من المفترض أن تتوهج بهدوء. هي لا تتكلم.

كنت مندهشًا. هل كان ذلك صحيحًا؟ عدت إلى المنزل لأقوم بدراسة من الكتاب المقدس. لم يمضِ وقت طويل حتى وجدت آيات مثل متى 4:23: «وكان يسوع يطوف جميع الجليل، يعلم في مجامعهم، وينادي ببشارة ملكوت، ويبرئ كل مرض وكل علّة بين الشعب.» ثم في متى 9، عندما «رأى الجموع فعطف عليهم لأنهم كانوا متعبين ومبعثرين كغنم لا راعي لها. ثم قال لتلاميذه: إن الحصاد كثير والعمال قليلون. فصلّوا إذًا إلى رب الحصاد أن يرسل عمالًا إلى حصاده» (متى 9:36-38).

يبدو لي أنه حيثما ذهب يسوع، كان يتحدث إلى الناس عن الملكوت. رأيت أناسًا يشهدون عن الله، لكن أحيانًا بطريقة مسيئة. فهل يعني ذلك أننا لا يجب أن نشهد؟ إذا قرأت سفر أعمال الرسل، فذلك تقريبًا كل ما تراه—إنجيل يخرج! في رواية واحدة أسرَّت السلطات التلاميذ وقالت لهم إنهم يمكن أن يذهبوا أحرارًا لو صمَّت أفواههم. ومع ذلك، قال التلاميذ إنهم لا يستطيعون. «لأننا لا نستطيع أن لا نتكلم بما رأينا وسمعنا» (أعمال 4:20). في وقت لاحق صمتوا—بالموت.

في وقت لاحق سمعت عن هؤلاء الناس الذين يدعون أنابابتيست. كلما درست عنهم، بدأت أرى كيف أنهم أيضًا لم يسكتوا. طلبت نسخة من The Martyr’s Mirror وذهلت عندما قرأت عن هؤلاء الناس الذين عاشوا مثل التلاميذ. لقد حققوا ما قاله يسوع، «وستبغضكم جميع الناس من أجل اسمي: أما من ثابر إلى المنتهى فهو يخلص» (متّى 10:22). وفي رومية 8:36، «كما هو مكتوب: من أجلك نُقتَل كل النهار، نُحسَب كغنم للمذبح.»

إخوتي وأخواتي الأعزاء، أعتقد أن النار تخبو. أسمع العديد من شعبنا الأنابابتيست يتحدثون عن العيش حياة هادئة ومسالمَة. يقول لنا يسوع في مثل الزارع: «أما الذي قبل البذر بين الشوك فهو الذي يسمع الكلمة، ثم تأتي هموم هذا العالم وخداع الغنى وتختنق الكلمة وتصبح بلا ثمر» (متى 13:22). هل يمكن أن يكون هذا هو حال كثيرين منا؟ نعيش في الأرض الحرة أميركا حيث يبدو أن المال سهل الحصول. هل من الممكن أننا خدعنا بثروتنا وبهموم هذا العالم؟ هل أصبحنا مثل العالم لتجنب الاضطهاد من قِبَله؟

منذ سنوات عديدة، هربت مجموعة من الأنابابتيست من الاضطهاد وانتقلوا إلى بلد كانت فيه الاضطهادات أقل. فتحوا متجر أثاث ليعيلوا أنفسهم، لكنهم لم يتمكنوا من بيع أي أثاث لأنهم كانوا الأنابابتيست المكروهون. سرعان ما أصبحت الحالة يائسة لأنهم لم يكن لديهم مال لشراء الطعام. في يومٍ ما دخل رجل ثري إلى المتجر. توقف كل العمال عما يفعلون. ظنوا في أنفسهم: «ربما سيشتري هذا الرجل شيئًا وسنستطيع أن نأكل!» اقترب أخ مسن من الزبون المحتمل وسأله إن كان يعرف يسوع. بعد حديث قصير خرج الرجل غاضبًا من المتجر. سأل العمال الجائعون الرجل المسن لماذا أخاف الزبون الوحيد وقد خيفتهم فرصتهم الوحيدة للبيع. شرح لهم أن معرفة هذا الرجل بيسوع كانت أهم بكثير من أن يكسبوا بعض المال.

في عقيدة الأنابابتيست الأوائل، كان إنجيل يسوع هو الأولوية. كما في سفر أعمال الرسل، لم يستطيعوا إلا أن يشهدوا بما رأوا وسمعوا. وهم أيضًا «كانوا يُقتَلون كل النهار».

فما الذي نفعل به بشأن الآية عن الحياة الهادئة والمسالمَة؟ توجد الآية في 1 تيموثاوس 2:1-2: «أُشَجِّعُ إذًا أن تُقام أولا كل الطلبات والدعوات والشفعات والشكر من أجل جميع الناس، من أجل الملوك، ومن أجل جميع الذين هم في سُلطان، لكي نمضي حياة هادئة ومسالمَة في كل تقوى ووقار.» ماذا كان يقصد الرسول بولس عندما كتب هذا؟ هل كان يعني أننا يجب أن نسكت عن الإنجيل ولا نتحدى خطيئًا أبدًا؟ من الصعب أن نصدق أن بولس يخبرنا أن نفعل شيئًا لم يفعله هو أبدًا، وشيئًا لم يفعله المسيح نفسه. في الواقع، لم يكن أحد في الكتابات الذي اتبع الله صامتًا بشأن إيمانه. في قصص عديدة للمسيحيين الأوائل الذين اعتُقلوا بسبب إيمانهم، كان السلطات تتوسل إليهم أن يصمتوا فقط! لكنهم رفضوا، كما فعل التلاميذ. واختروا الموت أيضًا بدلاً من حياة هادئة ومسالمَة.

شاب أنابابتيست اعتُقل وترك وراءه زوجته الحبيبة منتظرة مولودهم الأول. انتظرت السلطات حتى وُلد الطفل ثم أحضروا الرضيع إلى الأب الجديد في السجن. قالوا له إنه الآن أب ويمكنه العودة إلى المنزل ليكون مع زوجته وابنه. كان يمكنه حتى أن يستمر في الإيمان بنفس الطريقة، لكنه كان عليه أن يصمت وألا يتكلم ضد الخطيئة في كنيسة الدولة. رفض الأب الشاب. بالنسبة إليه لم يكن الصمت خيارًا. أحرقوه على الوتد.

فماذا تعني 1 تيموثاوس 2:1-2؟ يبدو أن المسيحيين في الكتاب والمسيحية الأولى كانوا كلُّ همّهم نشر الإنجيل، كلُّ همّهم كنيسة المسيح. كانوا يخرجون ينادون بالإنجيل، يعقدون اجتماعات في الجبال والغابات أو في أي مكان يجتمع فيه الناس. كانت تلك حياتهم. في الآية في 1 تيموثاوس 2، يقول بولس إن علينا أن نصلي أن تسمح لنا السلطات أن نعيش في سلام لكي ننشر الإنجيل. على المسيحيين أن يخرجوا لينشروا الكلمة ويتقدموا إلى الملكوت. دعاؤنا أن تسمح لنا السلطات بالعيش في سلام، بينما نخدم أمير السلام.

اليوم من السهل أن تكون مسيحيًا إذا استقريت وعشت حياة هادئة ومسالمَة، دون أن تتحدى خاطئًا أو تصحح أخًا. لكن من قال إن الأمر سيكون سهلًا؟

عندما كنا نعيش في هايتي، علمنا كنيستنا عن ثمن اتباع يسوع. كان من المذهل أن نسمع شهادات الهايتيين وهم يطبقون تعليم يسوع على حياتهم. في إحدى المرات أخبرنا عضوان أنهما على وشك فقدان وظيفتيهما بسبب اتباع الإنجيل. أن يسمعهما يقفان بثبات من أجل اتباع الحق أسعدني. أخبرتني أخت أخرى في الكنيسة أن المدرسة التي تذهب إليها أطفالها كان عليهم فيها ارتداء زي مدرسي والبنات مطالبات بارتداء بنطلون. عندما أرسلت ابنتها إلى المدرسة بفستان محتشم، عادت ومعها مذكرة من المديرة تقول لها ألا تعيد إرسال ابنتها إلى المدرسة وهي ترتدي ذلك الشيء.

Someone once said “When hope is alive, the night is less dark, the solitude less deep, and fear less acute.” When I worked in a prison as an assistant chaplain, I would sit with the condemned men and listen as they talked of their plight. Almost without exception, all spoke of hoping to get out of prison one day. Even if they had a life sentence, they hoped to get out.

I have spoken to people who do not confess to be born again, but still hope to go to heaven. These people dare not leave off hoping. Their hope is based upon their own hope! A diet on that kind of hope is a slim diet for sure! This reasoning reminds me of Jesus' words in John 10:1-2 about entering the sheepfold. “But he that entereth in by the door is the shepherd of the sheep.” People build their hope for heaven on many shaky things. Some base their hope on having been baptized in a certain church. Some hope in their church membership. Some people hope in their good works, while still others hope in their hope. The Bible, however, says, “. . . except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God” (John 3:3).

There is a true hope and a false hope. The false hope is “climbing up some other way,” but true hope is “he that entereth in by the door.”

“For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope: for what a man seeth, why doth he yet hope for?” (Romans 8:24). This word hope means “with anticipation or great expectation.” Could we say that we are saved by great expectation? Yes, we can. “Labour not for the meat which perisheth, but for that meat which endureth unto everlasting life, which the Son of man shall give unto you: for him hath God the Father sealed” (John 6:27). This seems to be a contradiction of sorts. Are we not saved by grace? Yes, we are saved by grace through faith (Ephesians 2:8). Then what is this being saved by hope and laboring for the “meat which endureth unto everlasting life”?

“Then they said unto him, what shall we do, that we might work the works of God?” Jesus answered and said unto them, “this is the work of God, that ye believe on him whom he hath sent” (John 6:28-29). It is only by grace that we are saved, but as this passage suggests, grace sets a condition. The condition of grace is that we believe on Him. Another condition of salvation is repentance (Mark 1:15), while another is cross-bearing. “Whosoever will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross and follow me” (Mark 8:34).

Everything we would do for Christ, whether believing, repenting, or cross-bearing, is by grace. Whatever we have, or do, is because of Him. We do not work for our salvation, for Christ Himself said, “It is finished.” We have nothing to hope for if we do not meet the conditions of our salvation. Once we receive the Lord Jesus as Saviour, then “hope maketh not ashamed” (Romans 5:5).

As Christ becomes alive in us, we love Him and choose to obey Him. Jesus becomes more precious to us as we mature in our Christian life. As our relationship grows, our expectation grows as well. The more we get to know Him, the more we look forward to being in His presence. As our anticipation of seeing Him grows, we try to do all things possible to please Him. Our great eagerness keeps us from becoming weary, thus, “we are saved by hope.”

Is your hope like the one who “climbeth up some other way,” or like, “he that entereth in by the door”? Do you have a basis for your hope or is it an empty hope that has no foundation?

I trust you are growing up “. . . into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ” (Ephesians 4:15).

I hope you might grow just a little more, so your expectation of seeing Christ might grow as well. The testimony of this expectation is, “. . . in this we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house which is from heaven” (2 Corinthians 5:2).

有人曾说：“当盼望在时，夜色就不那么黑暗，孤独就不那么深沉，恐惧也不那么强烈。” 当我在监狱担任助理牧师时，我常与被判死刑的人同坐，倾听他们谈论自己的困境。几乎毫无例外，他们都谈到希望有一天能离开监狱。即便被判无期徒刑，他们也希望能出狱。

我也与那些不承认自己重生的人交谈过，但他们仍然希望能去天堂。这些人不敢停止盼望。他们的盼望建立在自己的“希望”之上！倚靠那种盼望的食粮确实很薄弱！这种推理让我想起耶稣在约翰福音10:1-2关于进入羊圈的话：“惟有从门进去的，才是牧人。羊听他的声音，他也按着名叫出自己的羊来。”人们把得天国的盼望建立在许多不稳固的事物上。有些人把盼望寄托在曾在某教会受洗上；有些人寄望于他们的教会会籍；有些人盼望自己的善行；另一些人则盼望于自己的“希望”。然而圣经说：“……若不是重生，就不能见神的国”（约翰福音3:3）。

有真实的盼望，也有虚假的盼望。虚假的盼望是“从别处爬上去的”，真实的盼望是“从门进去的”。

“我们得救是在于盼望；只是所看见的盼望就不是盼望；因为谁还盼望他所看见的呢？”（罗马书8:24）。这里的盼望意谓“怀着期待或极大的期望”。我们可以说我们是靠极大的期待得救吗？是的，我们可以。 “不要为那必坏的食物劳力，要为那存到永生的食物劳力，就是人子要赐给你们的；因为那被父神印证的人就是他。”（约翰福音6:27）。这似乎在某种程度上构成矛盾。我们不是靠恩典得救吗？是的，我们是靠恩典，凭着信得救（以弗所书2:8）。那么这“靠盼望得救”和为“存到永生的食物劳力”是什么意思呢？

“他们就问他说，我们当行什么，才能行 神的工呢？”耶稣回答说：“信他所差来的，这就是神的工。”（约翰福音6:28-29）。我们是单靠恩典得救，但正如这段经文所示，恩典设定了一个条件。恩典的条件是我们信他。得救的另一个条件是悔改（马可福音1:15），还有一个是背十字架。“若有人要跟从我，就当舍己，背起他的十字架来跟从我。”（马可福音8:34）。

我们为基督所做的一切——无论是信、悔改或背十字架——都是出于恩典。我们所有的一切或所作所为，都是因着他。我们不是靠行为挣得救恩，因为基督自己说过：“成了。”如果我们不符合得救的条件，就没有任何可以指望的。我们一旦接受主耶稣为救主，那么“盼望不至于羞耻”（罗马书5:5）。

当基督在我们里面活过来时，我们就爱他并选择顺服他。随着我们在基督徒生命中的成长，耶稣对我们越发宝贵。随着关系的增长，我们的期待也随之增长。我们越认识他，就越盼望与他同在。对见他的期盼越强烈，我们就越努力行一切能讨他喜悦的事。我们那强烈的渴望使我们不致疲乏，因此“我们是靠盼望得救”。

你的盼望是像那“从别处爬上去”的人，还是像“从门进去的”人？你的盼望有根基，还是一个没有根基的空洞盼望？

我盼望你在“凡事上长入他──元首基督”（以弗所书4:15）。

我希望你能再长进一些，使你见基督的盼望也随之增长。这盼望的见证是：“我们在这外邦的帐棚里叹息，切望披上从天上来的家园。”（哥林多后书5:2）。
